MaterialSystem.description: YBa2Cu3O7−δ (YBCO) epitaxial thick films (2.4 µm) on LaMnO3/MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3/Hastelloy templates; BaHfO3 (BHO) perovskite nanocrystals (3–10 nm) are mono-dispersively embedded and act as isotropic artificial pinning centers. After high-temperature growth BHO coarsening is size-dependent (3 nm → 20 nm, 5.5 nm → 7 nm), generating spherical incoherent particles, local strain fields, Y248 intergrowths and stacking faults that collectively enhance vortex pinning without degrading epitaxial c-axis texture.

TunningMethod.description: Performance is optimized by synergistically tuning the pristine BHO nanocrystal size and concentration to control final particle size/density, thereby matching the temperature- and field-dependent coherence length for maximal flux pinning while minimizing self-field Ic degradation.

strategies.tuning strategies: Pre-formed BHO nanocrystals (3–10 nm) are added at 5–20 mol% to modulate the volume fraction and size distribution of non-superconducting pinning phases; smaller pristine sizes yield higher number density but suffer severe coarsening (6.3× for 3 nm), whereas 5.5 nm gives the smallest final size (7 ± 3 nm) and highest particle density (20.5e21 m−3), providing the most effective pinning centers.
strategies.tuning effects: 10 mol% 5.5 nm BHO raises in-field Jc to 20.8 MA cm−2 at 1 T, 4.2 K and produces the highest lifting factor (10.9 at 1 T, 4.2 K) while keeping self-field Ic above 800 A/12 mm.

strategies.tuning strategies: A 200–300 nm pure YBCO seed layer is first deposited to ensure epitaxial growth of the subsequent BHO-doped layer; limited BHO/YBCO lattice mismatch introduces local strain and stacking faults that act as additional pinning sites without disrupting the overall c-axis texture.
strategies.tuning effects: Homogeneous spherical BHO particles (7–11 nm) are embedded without agglomeration, maintaining high epitaxial quality and enabling record Jc enhancement at low temperatures.

strategies.tuning strategies: Geometric phase analysis reveals non-uniform εxx and εyy strain fields around BHO particles and Y248 intergrowths; these elastic strain regions create nanoscale potential landscapes that supplement core pinning, especially effective at low temperatures where coherence length is short.
strategies.tuning effects: Strain-related pinning contributes to the superior 5.5 nm BHO performance, shifting the peak normalized Jc (η) to higher fields (Bp ≈ 3 T at 4.2 K).

strategies.tuning strategies: Reel-to-reel MOD processing on biaxially textured LaMnO3/MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3/Hastelloy substrates preserves sharp biaxial texture in 2.4 µm thick films even after multiple coatings and high-temperature growth; BHO addition does not degrade the c-axis alignment, ensuring long-range percolative current paths.
strategies.tuning effects: High self-field Ic (>800 A/12 mm) is retained at 77 K for 5 mol% BHO, while textured growth allows full utilization of aligned pinning centers under applied field.

strategies.tuning strategies: By keeping BHO particles small (≤11 nm) and uniformly dispersed, grain boundary contamination and weak-link behavior are minimized; the optimal 5.5 nm BHO case exhibits the least Ic degradation with increasing concentration, indicating suppressed grain boundary scattering.
strategies.tuning effects: Linear Ic decrease with concentration is weakest for 5.5 nm BHO, enabling 10 mol% loading without catastrophic loss of connectivity, thus balancing pinning strength and grain boundary transparency.

ExperimentTech.description: Low-fluorine metal–organic deposition (MOD) with industrial reel-to-reel coating, polyol solvothermal synthesis of mono-dispersed BHO nanocrystals, multistep epitaxial growth (785 °C) with intermediate cooling; cross-sectional HRTEM/STEM-Z, GPA strain mapping, hysteresis-loop Jc (Bean model), and transport Ic (M-Corder) measurements.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Polyol solvothermal BHO nanocrystal synthesis; low-fluorine MOD; reel-to-reel coating; multistep epitaxial growth with self-seeding layer
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: HRTEM, STEM-Z, GPA strain mapping, XRD, FIB cross-sectioning
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: SQUID-VSM hysteresis loops (Bean model), transport Ic (M-Corder), angular Ic(θ) at 77 K

Application.description: High-field, low-temperature magnet applications require coated conductors that maintain high critical current density (Jc) in magnetic fields up to 9 T while retaining acceptable self-field performance at 77 K for cryogenic power devices.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field magnets, cryogenic power cables, superconducting coils operating at 4.2–50 K under 3–9 T
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc = 20.8 MA cm−2 at 1 T, 4.2 K; Jc = 8.7 MA cm−2 at 1 T, 30 K; Ic = 827 A/12 mm at 77 K, self-field; lifting factor 10.9 at 1 T, 4.2 K

MaterialSystem.description: The system consists of a bilayer REBCO coated conductor: a lower EuBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ (EuBCO) film containing c-axis-inclined BaHfO₃ nano-rods (BHO NRs, ~40 nm long) and an upper YBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ (YBCO) film embedding randomly distributed Y₂O₃ nano-particles (YO NPs, 10–30 nm tablet-like). Both layers grow epitaxially on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy C-276 with strong biaxial texture, yielding a single-crystal-like matrix that minimizes high-angle grain boundaries.

TunningMethod.description: A bilayer architecture is designed so that c-axis-correlated BHO nano-rods (Eu-NR layer) selectively reinforce Jc near B∥c (θ≈0°), while randomly oriented YO nano-particles (Y-NP layer) preferentially raise Jc near B∥ab (θ≈90°). By linearly superposing the two pinning landscapes the overall Jc(θ) anisotropy is minimized; the volume fraction of each layer provides an additional knob for further fine-tuning under given (T,B) service windows.

strategies.tuning strategies: Introduce 2–5 mol% BaHfO₃ into EuBCO to form c-axis-inclined nano-rods that create strong correlated pinning along the c-axis, raising Jc(θ≈0°) and shifting the irreversibility field to higher values.
strategies.tuning effects: Enhances low-field Jc by ~2× at 65 K, 3 T, B∥c and enlarges the usable B–T window for motor applications.

strategies.tuning strategies: Add 5–25 mol% excess Y in YBCO target to precipitate fine Y₂O₃ nano-particles that act as isotropic point-like pins, selectively boosting Jc when the field lies close to the ab-plane (θ≈90°).
strategies.tuning effects: Produces a broad Jc peak at 85–90° and compensates the intrinsic mass anisotropy, cutting the anisotropy factor A from ~1.1 to <0.55 under 3 T, 77 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Stack YBCO(YO-NP) atop EuBCO(BHO-NR) without intermediate spacer; the clean hetero-interface preserves epitaxy and enables parallel current paths, allowing Kirchhoff summation of layer Jc values.
strategies.tuning effects: Realizes complementary pinning in one tape; experimental IEu-NR/Y-NP c,1 cm is reproduced by 0.535 IY-NP c,1 cm + 1.05 IEu-NR c,1 cm, validating the concept.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3 buffer stack to impose sharp biaxial texture (Δφ<5°) on both EuBCO and YBCO layers, eliminating weak-link grain boundaries and enabling full utilization of APCs.
strategies.tuning effects: Maintains high in-field Jc (>1e4 A cm⁻² at 77 K, 3 T) and allows the APC design to dominate the angular response rather than grain-boundary limitations.

strategies.tuning strategies: Keep individual layer thickness ≤1.65 µm and total bilayer ≤3.1 µm to limit residual tensile strain; post-anneal at 300–400 °C in flowing O₂ relaxes lattice mismatch between EuBCO and YBCO and optimizes carrier doping.
strategies.tuning effects: Prevents crack formation under >50 GN m⁻³ Lorentz force and preserves Tc (94 K) close to the optimum of each constituent layer.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were fabricated by industrial-scale pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) using a 300 Hz LEAP-300C laser on 4 mm-wide IBAD tapes. Microstructure was resolved by aberration-corrected STEM combined with EDS elemental mapping to verify bilayer registry and APC morphology. Critical current density was measured on 50 µm micro-bridges via four-probe DC transport in fields up to 15 T and temperatures 65–81 K with automated θ-rotation, enabling full Jc(B,T,θ) surface acquisition.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) with multi-target carousel; 2 µm Ag sputter cap; ex-situ oxygen anneal
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Cross-sectional STEM/HAADF, EDS mapping, FFT of lattice images
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: DC four-probe Jc(θ) under 15 T cryogen-free magnet, Cernox thermometry, Hall-sensor angle tracking

Application.description: Electric aircraft and ship propulsion motors require REBCO tapes that carry high, isotropic current at 65–77 K and ≤3 T to simplify coil design and minimize AC losses. The bilayer tape achieves A<0.55 under these conditions, offering a ready-to-scale route for long-length conductors processed in a single multi-turn PLD pass.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-temperature superconducting motors and generators cooled by pumped liquid nitrogen
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc>1e4 A cm⁻² at 77 K, 3 T, B∥c; Jc anisotropy factor A<0.55 at 65–77 K, ≤3 T; irreversibility field ≈9 T at 77 K

MaterialSystem.description: YBa₂Cu₃Oᵧ (YBCO) thick films grown on IBAD-MgO metal substrates by vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) assisted PLD. Films exhibit strong c-axis texture (Δω ≤ 0.72°, Δϕ ≤ 1.49°) and very low a-axis grain ratio (< 2.8 %). Tc ≥ 90 K for all thicknesses (0.94–3.7 µm). No intentional dopants; minor Cu-rich droplets from residual Ba-Cu-O liquid phase act as benign secondary precipitates.

TunningMethod.description: Thickness of the superconducting layer is systematically increased (0.94 → 3.7 µm) while high c-axis texture is preserved via VLS growth. Thicker films enlarge the pinning correlation length L, which becomes comparable to or larger than d at 60–77 K and several Tesla; this raises the effective pinning potential U₀ and suppresses thermally activated flux creep, yielding a >10× higher Jc at 70 K, 2.5 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain stoichiometric YBCO without artificial pinning additives; rely on intrinsic disorder and Cu-rich droplets from residual Ba-Cu-O liquid to provide weak pinning centers.
strategies.tuning effects: Avoids secondary-phase overdose that would degrade texture; droplets contribute modest extra pinning without deteriorating Tc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ VLS growth mode to sustain excellent c-axis orientation (Δω ≈ 0.63–0.72°) and suppress a-axis grains (< 0.03 %) even when thickness reaches 3.7 µm, whereas conventional PLD suffers misorientation.
strategies.tuning effects: Minimizes high-angle grain boundaries, thereby reducing weak-link limitation and allowing thickness scaling of Jc to be fully exploited.

strategies.tuning strategies: Keep a thin Ba-Cu-O liquid layer at the growth front throughout vapor deposition; this liquid mediates low-supersaturation epitaxy and heals surface defects.
strategies.tuning effects: Delays transition to rough vapor-phase growth, maintaining smooth surfaces (low roughness) and high crystallinity up to ~1.4 µm; beyond this, liquid depletion is mitigated by optimized deposition time.

strategies.tuning strategies: By increasing film thickness, the pinning correlation volume elongates along the c-axis, effectively decreasing the relative contribution of individual grain boundaries to flux creep.
strategies.tuning effects: Macroscopic Jc becomes less sensitive to local weak links; experimentally, thicker films show smaller Jc reduction with field at 77 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: VLS low-temperature liquid phase relaxes epitaxial strain during growth, limiting residual tensile stress that could crack thick films.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables crack-free 3.7 µm films with Tc ≈ 90.6 K, permitting full utilization of thickness-enhanced pinning potential without mechanical degradation.

ExperimentTech.description: Thick YBCO films are fabricated by a hybrid VLS-PLD process (KrF laser, 860–940 °C, 53–200 Pa O₂). Crystal quality is quantified by XRD 2θ-ω, rocking curves and ϕ-scans. Surface precipitates are mapped via SEM-EDX. Composition & thickness verified by ICP-OES. Magnetization relaxation measured with SQUID (30–77 K, c-axis field) and converted to E–J curves; apparent pinning potential U₀* extracted from ln(t) decay.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition assisted vapor-liquid-solid (VLS-PLD) tri-phase epitaxy
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (2θ-ω, rocking curve, ϕ-scan), SEM-EDX elemental mapping, ICP-OES thickness/composition
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: SQUID magnetometer magnetic-relaxation → E–J characteristics; four-probe Tc

Application.description: REBCO coated conductors are targeted for liquid-nitrogen-temperature magnets and cables where operation above 60 K under fields of several Tesla is required. Enhancing Jc at 77 K, 2–3 T directly translates to higher engineering current capacity and reduced refrigeration cost.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled high-field magnets, fault-current limiters and fusion reactors
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(77 K, 2.5 T) increases from 1e8 A m⁻² (0.94 µm) to 1.14e9 A m⁻² (3.7 µm) (>10× gain); U₀*(77 K, 2 T) rises with thickness, indicating stronger flux pinning.

MaterialSystem.description: Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7−δ (Gd0.5Yb0.5BCO) REBCO superconducting films deposited on buffered Hastelloy tapes. The films exhibit high-quality biaxial texture with c-axis orientation. Zr doping induces elongated BaZrO3 nanorods (length >100 nm, width ~6 nm) while suppressing dense vertically aligned BaCuO2 nanorods (~20–50 nm). RE2O3 nanoprecipitates are also present. Increasing Zr content expands the REBCO c-axis lattice and reduces Tc.

TunningMethod.description: Heavy Zr doping (15–25 mol%) transforms the flux-pinning landscape from dense BaCuO2 nanorods to dense elongated BaZrO3 nanorods, enhancing Jc over low-to-medium fields while preserving high-field performance via residual BaCuO2 and hierarchical intrinsic pinning.

strategies.tuning strategies: Systematic increase of Zr content (5–25 mol%) in precursor to form BaZrO3 nanorods and suppress BaCuO2 nanorods.
strategies.tuning effects: BaZrO3 number density rises to 2.2e3 rods µm−2; BaCuO2 peak intensity drops 20-fold, eliminating vertical nanorods above 10 mol% Zr.

strategies.tuning strategies: Optimize RE:(Ba–Zr):Cu ratio (0.65:0.65:2.00:3.20) to balance matrix integrity and nanorod self-assembly while maintaining sharp REBCO/BaZrO3 interfaces.
strategies.tuning effects: Ensures elongated BaZrO3 nanorods grow >100 nm without disrupting REBCO matrix; prevents RE2O3 coarsening.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit nanoscale lattice mismatch between BaZrO3 and REBCO to create local strain fields that modulate oxygen content and enhance pinning.
strategies.tuning effects: Tc decreases linearly from 88.4 K to 86.1 K with 25 mol% Zr; strain-induced oxygen vacancies provide additional pinning sites.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain high-quality biaxial texture under heavy Zr doping by low deposition rate (90 nm min−1) and fixed 775 °C, 0.7 Torr O2.
strategies.tuning effects: No misoriented a-axis grains detected up to 25 mol% Zr; BaZrO3 (200) texture strengthens with Zr, preserving current path alignment.

strategies.tuning strategies: Minimize high-angle grain boundaries via epitaxial growth on IBAD-MgO buffered substrates, ensuring nanorods align along c-axis.
strategies.tuning effects: Reduces weak-link effect; correlated pinning peaks at B//c remain sharp, yielding Jc_min enhancement at 30 K and 5 T.

ExperimentTech.description: Liquid-delivery MOCVD grown 0.55 µm films on 5-layer buffered Hastelloy; 2D-XRD quantifies phase evolution; cross-sectional and plan-view TEM resolve nanorod morphology and density; transport and magnetization Jc measured 4–77 K, 0–14 T.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Liquid-delivery metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: 2D-X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), electron probe microanalysis (EPMA)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe transport Jc, Quantum Design PPMS magnetization Jc (Bean model), angular Jc(θ) at 30 K & 20 K

Application.description: Low-temperature (4–20 K) high-field magnets for compact fusion and particle accelerators require high Jc across 0–30 T; heavy Zr-doped GdYbBCO tapes deliver superior Jc up to 20.5 T while undoped tape excels >20 T.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Ultra-high-field fusion magnets and accelerator dipoles operating below 20 K
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(4 K, 5 T) ≈ 35 MA cm−2 for 15 mol% Zr; Jc(4 K, 20 T) ≈ 6.8 MA cm−2 for 25 mol% Zr; Jc(4 K, 30 T) ≈ 5.5 MA cm−2 for undoped tape

MaterialSystem.description: REBCO superconducting matrix with embedded nano-scaled BaCeO3/CeO2 composite pinning centers; BaCeO3 exhibits temperature-dependent polymorphism (orthorhombic Pmna → Imma → rhombohedral R-3c → cubic Pm-3m) while CeO2 retains cubic fluorite structure, both phases < 40 nm.

TunningMethod.description: A reverse co-precipitation route exploiting acid-base and redox chemistry of Ba²⁺ and Ce³⁺/Ce⁴⁺ avoids carbonate/organic precipitants, yielding nano-sized BaCeO3–CeO2 mixture that functions as engineered pinning centers; incomplete Ba precipitation is tolerated because CeO2 itself is an accepted pinning phase.

strategies.tuning strategies: Eliminate carbonate/oxalate precipitants to suppress BaCO3 formation; instead use NH3/H2O2 to precipitate Ba²⁺ as hydroxide and re-oxidize Ce³⁺→CeO2, creating a dual-phase BaCeO3+CeO2 nanocomposite that provides heterogeneous pinning sites.
strategies.tuning effects: Residual BaCO3 drops below XRD/Raman detection at 1000 °C; dual-phase mixture still acceptable for pinning since CeO2 is itself a known pinning oxide.

strategies.tuning strategies: Keep crystallite size ≤ 35 nm (BaCeO3) and ≤ 35 nm (CeO2) by annealing at 800–1000 °C; nanometric grains maximize grain-boundary area within REBCO matrix, increasing defect density for vortex pinning without blocking current percolation paths.
strategies.tuning effects: Williamson–Hall analysis gives 25→33 nm (BaCeO3) and 19→35 nm (CeO2) when temperature rises 800→1000 °C, maintaining effective nano-pinning scale.

strategies.tuning strategies: Directly precipitate oxide/hydroxide nanoparticles that are crystallographically compatible with REBCO (perovskite BaCeO3 and fluorite CeO2), ensuring low interfacial energy and coherent or semi-coherent interfaces that minimize weak-link behavior.
strategies.tuning effects: No secondary reaction layers (e.g. BaCO3) at interface after 1000 °C treatment, promoting clean, epitaxy-ready surfaces for REBCO growth.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use rapid cooling (10 °C/min) after 60 min anneal to freeze high-temperature cubic/rhombohedral polymorphs of BaCeO3, introducing local lattice mismatch strain fields that act as additional pinning centers without macroscopic film cracking.
strategies.tuning effects: Controlled thermal quench preserves nanoscale strain fields around BaCeO3/CeO2 inclusions, enhancing vortex pinning energy.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ nano-sized, phase-pure crystallites that can be dispersed in REBCO precursor inks; during REBCO epitaxy these particles align with the matrix c-axis, creating columnar or random nanoparticle arrays that preserve biaxial texture of the superconducting film.
strategies.tuning effects: Absence of BaCO3 prevents texture degradation, allowing transferred REBCO film to maintain high in-plane and out-of-plane alignment.

ExperimentTech.description: Reverse co-precipitation (innovative carbonate-free) for powder synthesis; XRD Rietveld & Williamson–Hall for phase/size quantification; Raman for carbonate trace detection; SEM for morphology; coupled DTA/TG-MS for thermal decomposition tracking.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Reverse co-precipitation (Ba/Ce nitrate → NH3/H2O2), 800–1000 °C anneal
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: XRD (Co Kα), Raman spectroscopy (Nd:YAG 532 nm), SEM (FIB-SEM)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: DTA/TG-MS (10 K min⁻¹, air) for evolved gas analysis

Application.description: Nano-additive for introduction of artificial pinning centers into REBCO coated conductors to raise in-field critical current density at intermediate temperatures and magnetic fields.
Application.ApplicationScenario: REBCO coated-conductor tapes for high-field magnets and fault-current limiters
Application.ApplicationIndex: Engineered pinning centers (BaCeO3+CeO2, 19–35 nm) targeting enhanced Jc(B,T) performance

MaterialSystem.description: Gd0.5Yb0.5Ba2Cu3O7-δ (GdYbBCO) coated conductors grown on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes. The matrix is c-axis oriented (Δω≈2°, Δφ≈4°) with c-lattice parameter 11.63–11.67 Å. Self-assembled (011)-BaCuO2 nanorods (≈7 nm wide, ≈52 nm long, density ≈3700 μm⁻² per layer) and (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodot layers (5–9 nm, tilted ≤7° from ab-plane) form a hierarchical pinning architecture. Lattice mismatch between BaCuO2 and REBCO is minimized to ≈5.6 %, producing coherent, dislocation-free interfaces.
MaterialSystem.dopants: none (self-assembled BaCuO2 and (Gd,Yb)2O3 secondary phases only)

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic composition tuning of Cu/Ba and (Gd+Yb)/Ba atomic ratios governs the self-assembly of BaCuO2 nanorods and (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodots. Optimal ratios (Cu/Ba=1.19, RE/Ba=0.65) minimize lattice mismatch, maximize nanorod aspect ratio and density, and create a bidirectional defect landscape that suppresses vortex motion across 4–77 K and 0–14 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Fix RE/Ba=0.65 and vary Cu/Ba from 1.15 to 1.21; only Cu/Ba=1.19 yields dense, vertically aligned (011)-BaCuO2 nanorods, while higher Cu forms CuO/RECuO2 surface precipitates that block nanorod growth.
strategies.tuning effects: Maximizes c-axis-correlated pinning centers; Jc(4 K, 5 T) reaches 13.2 MA cm⁻² and power-law exponent α drops to 0.39.

strategies.tuning strategies: Fix Cu/Ba=1.19 and vary RE/Ba from 0.55 to 0.75; increasing RE/Ba increases (Gd,Yb)2O3 nanodot density but shortens BaCuO2 nanorods by hindering self-assembly, raising their diameter from 6.8 nm to 10 nm.
strategies.tuning effects: Creates layered REO nanodots that enhance ab-plane pinning; optimal RE/Ba=0.65 balances long nanorods and dense nanodots, yielding highest B*=551 mT and Fp=670 GN m⁻³ at 4 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Minimize lattice mismatch between (011)-BaCuO2 and REBCO matrix (|f1/f3|=1.42) to maintain coherent, dislocation-free interfaces; mismatch increases to 6.6 % when composition deviates, introducing interfacial dislocations and degrading nanorod continuity.
strategies.tuning effects: Coherent interfaces enable elastic strain accommodation without misfit dislocations, stabilizing long nanorods and reducing α.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain sharp c-axis texture (Δω<3°, Δφ<5°) via identical IBAD-MgO buffered substrates for all samples; texture quality is insensitive to composition but essential for epitaxial nanorod alignment.
strategies.tuning effects: Ensures vertical alignment of BaCuO2 nanorods along c-axis, maximizing pinning when field B//c.

strategies.tuning strategies: Allow controlled elastic strain (≈3 % tensile in BCO, ≈-12 % compressive in REBCO) at coherent nanorod/matrix interfaces; strain fields drive self-assembly of nanorods along c-axis while avoiding plastic relaxation.
strategies.tuning effects: Strain field guides nanorod formation direction and prevents formation of misoriented precipitates, maintaining high pinning efficiency up to 14 T.

ExperimentTech.description: Reel-to-reel MOCVD on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes for uniform 0.54 μm thick films; precursor molar ratios precisely varied to target Cu/Ba and RE/Ba. Microstructure quantified by cross-sectional TEM (≥100 nanorods per sample), 2D-XRD at χ=45° to resolve BaCuO2 orientation, and GPA strain mapping. Transport Jc measured by four-probe 1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion at 4–77 K, 0–5 T, with angular rotation 0–180°; magnetization Jc up to 14 T using Bean model calibrated against transport data.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: reel-to-reel metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), 2D-XRD, energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), geometric phase analysis (GPA) strain mapping
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: four-probe transport critical current (1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion), angular-dependent Ic, magnetization hysteresis (PPMS, Bean model)

Application.description: Ultrahigh-field (>20 T) low-temperature (4 K) magnets for fusion reactors, high-energy particle accelerators and NMR systems require conductors that retain high Jc with slow field decay. Optimized GdYbBCO tapes outperform 15 % Zr-doped REBCO above 20 T due to smaller α=0.39 and dense hierarchical pinning, enabling compact, high-field coils.
Application.ApplicationScenario: ultrahigh-field fusion magnets and particle accelerator dipoles operating at 4 K and ≥20 T
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc_min=13.2 MA cm⁻² at 4 K, 5 T; power-law exponent α=0.39; B*=551 mT at 10 K; Fp_max=670 GN m⁻³ at 4 K, 5 T; Jc(4 K, >20 T) exceeds 15 % Zr-doped GdYBCO

MaterialSystem.description: Ternary (Sm,Eu,Gd)Ba2Cu3O7−δ (SEG-123) bulk superconductor with orthorhombic structure (c ≈ 11.74 Å) grown as single-domain by top-seeded infiltration growth in air; BaO2 addition suppresses RE/Ba substitution while Ag2O refines 211 particles and introduces extra pinning centers.
MaterialSystem.dopants: BaO2 (0–5 wt %), Ag2O (10 wt %), Pt (0.5 wt %)

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic optimization via BaO2-driven Ba-rich composition to suppress RE/Ba anti-site disorder (sharper Tc and stronger δTc pinning) and Ag2O-assisted liquid-phase engineering to create additional field-induced pinning centers, together doubling high-field Jc without losing high Tc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Systematic addition of BaO2 up to 4 wt % in SEG-211 precursor to enrich Ba content and suppress RE/Ba substitution.
strategies.tuning effects: Tc(onset) rises from 92.65 K to 94.57 K and ΔTc narrows by 71 % to 0.88 K; self-field Jc(77 K) increases 31 % to 33.55 kA cm−2.

strategies.tuning strategies: Co-doping 10 wt % Ag2O with the optimized BaO2 level to introduce molten Ag that releases oxygen and modifies local atmosphere.
strategies.tuning effects: High-field Jc(65 K, 3 T) jumps to 50.54 kA cm−2 (≈4.3× reference) while Tc stays >93 K and ΔTc remains <1.5 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employing separate liquid-source (Y-123 + Ba3Cu5O8) and SEG-211 pellets in TSIG to let liquid infiltrate and react homogeneously, avoiding residual liquid pools.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates macro-segregation and ensures uniform 211 distribution, preventing the liquid-inclusion defects seen when BaO2 exceeds 4 wt %.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintaining sub-micron 211 particles (mean 3.2–3.3 µm) via Pt and Ag2O refiners to increase 211/123 interface density.
strategies.tuning effects: Finer 211 particles act as effective flux-pinning sites, shifting pinning mechanism from δl- to stronger δTc-type (hmax 0.286→0.40).

strategies.tuning strategies: c-axis oriented Nd-123 seed and slow 0.2 °C h−1 growth window to secure single-domain epitaxy along  direction.
strategies.tuning effects: XRD shows only (00l) peaks; absence of spontaneous nucleation guarantees low-angle grain boundaries and high inter-grain Jc.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were fabricated by top-seeded infiltration growth in air; phase purity and texture verified by XRD, microstructure by FE-SEM, and superconducting properties (Tc, Jc) measured with SQUID magnetometry using extended Bean model.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Top-seeded infiltration growth (TSIG) in air with controlled oxygen annealing 450–350 °C
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (Cu-Kα), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: SQUID magnetometry (Tc at 1 mT, Jc from M–H loops up to 5 T via extended Bean model)

Application.description: Cost-effective batch production of high-performance REBCO bulks for liquid-nitrogen (77 K) and liquid-oxygen (90 K) operation in high-field permanent-magnet systems.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Compact superconducting permanent magnets, Maglev guidestars, trapped-field devices up to 3 T at 65–77 K

MaterialSystem.description: MOD-derived YBa2Cu3O7-δ (YBCO) coated conductors with embedded BaHfO3 (BHO) perovskite nanocrystals. BHO retains its cubic perovskite structure after growth and acts as three-dimensional isotropic artificial pinning centers; lattice mismatch creates nano-strain regions that further enhance vortex pinning without degrading the biaxial YBCO texture.
MaterialSystem.dopants: BaHfO3 (BHO) nanocrystals, 5.5 nm or 6.5 nm in diameter, 5–15 mol% vs. Y

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic optimization of BHO nanocrystal size and concentration to maximize low-temperature in-field Jc. A two-step film-growth protocol suppresses coarsening, while size selection avoids instability-driven particle growth that reduces pinning efficiency.

strategies.tuning strategies: Increase BHO concentration from 5 mol% to 15 mol% to raise the density of 3D artificial pinning centers, compensating for the limited number of flux lines at low temperature and high field.
strategies.tuning effects: At 30 K & 3 T, 15 mol% BHO yields 2.94-fold Jc enhancement versus pristine film; flux-pinning force reaches 4.9 GN m⁻³ at 4.2 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ a two-step growth (785 °C pre-growth + 785–795 °C final growth) to preserve monodisperse BHO nanocrystals and minimize interfacial coarsening, maintaining small final particle size within the 1.5 µm YBCO matrix.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables higher optimal BHO content (15 mol%) than conventional single-step routes (≈5 mol%) without film degradation, shifting Fp,max to higher fields.

strategies.tuning strategies: Select 6.5 nm BHO nanocrystals instead of 5.5 nm to avoid thermally driven coarsening that converts small unstable particles into fewer, larger pins with reduced pinning efficiency.
strategies.tuning effects: 6.5 nm BHO films exhibit superior Jc at 0–1 T and 4.2–30 K; 5.5 nm BHO suffers coarsening, giving 15–20% lower absolute Jc under the same conditions.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain sharp YBCO biaxial texture on LMO/MgO/Y2O3/Al2O3/Hastelloy architecture while embedding BHO nanocrystals, ensuring that added particles do not disrupt the c-axis alignment required for high current percolation.
strategies.tuning effects: Self-field Jc remains high (>2 MA cm⁻² at 77 K) even at 15 mol% BHO, indicating negligible texture degradation.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit nano-strain fields around coherent BHO particles to create additional local suppression of the order parameter, synergistically enhancing 3D flux pinning without introducing macroscopic residual stress that could crack the 1.5 µm thick film.
strategies.tuning effects: Contributes to the continuous rise of Fp with BHO content up to 15 mol% at 4.2 K, whereas at 77 K the optimal content is 10 mol% due to reduced elastic strain accommodation at higher temperature.

ExperimentTech.description: Continuous reel-to-reel LF-MOD coating on buffered Hastelloy; two-step crystallization to suppress coarsening. HRTEM/FIB for cross-sectional nanoparticle imaging; magnetometry-based Jc extraction via extended Bean model.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Low-fluorine metal-organic deposition (LF-MOD), reel-to-reel coating, two-step growth (785 °C pre-growth + 785–795 °C final growth), oxygen anneal 450 °C
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: HRTEM (JEOL JEM-2010F), FIB (FEI Helios Nanolab 600i) lamella preparation, EDS elemental mapping, XRD of BHO powders
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Quantum Design PPMS hysteresis loops, extended Bean model Jc calculation (a = b = 4 mm), flux-pinning force Fp = Jc × B

Application.description: High-field magnets, cables and rotating machinery require coated conductors that retain high current density (>2 MA cm⁻²) in fields of 3–7 T at 20–30 K; BHO-doped MOD-YBCO meets this demand with a 2.94× Jc boost at 30 K, 3 T.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Compact fusion magnets, high-field accelerator dipoles, cryo-cooled motors/generators
Application.ApplicationIndex: In-field Jc = 2.94× pristine (30 K, 3 T); Fp,max = 4.9 GN m⁻³ (4.2 K); self-field Jc > 2 MA cm⁻² (77 K)

MaterialSystem.description: The system consists of YBa2Cu3O7−δ (YBCO) high-temperature superconductor grown on flexible metallic substrates with LaMnO3−δ (LMO) buffer layers. The LMO buffer layer exhibits oxygen-deficient perovskite structure (space group Pm-3m) with lattice constant varying from 3.92 Å (oxygen-deficient) to 3.85 Å (oxygen-annealed), resulting in lattice mismatch with YBCO (a-b plane ~3.85 Å) decreasing from 1.85% to 0.06%. The oxygen vacancies (VO) in LMO cause lattice expansion and MnO6 octahedral distortion, while oxygen annealing induces lattice contraction through Mn3+→Mn4+ oxidation and VO reduction.

TunningMethod.description: The study synergistically optimizes YBCO superconducting performance by modulating LMO buffer layer oxygen stoichiometry through post-annealing in oxygen atmosphere. This strategy reduces lattice mismatch, suppresses a-axis oriented grains, and enhances c-axis epitaxial growth, ultimately improving critical current by ~20%.

strategies.tuning strategies: Post-annealing LMO films in oxygen atmosphere (500–620 °C, 0–2 h) to fill oxygen vacancies, oxidize Mn3+→Mn4+, and reduce VO concentration, thereby shortening Mn–O bonds and contracting lattice constant from 3.92 Å to 3.85 Å.
strategies.tuning effects: Lattice mismatch with YBCO decreases from 1.85% to 0.06%, enabling high-quality c-axis epitaxial growth and suppressing a-axis grains.

strategies.tuning strategies: Engineering LMO/YBCO interface by reducing lattice mismatch through oxygen-induced lattice contraction, which mitigates interfacial residual stress and misfit dislocation density.
strategies.tuning effects: Improved epitaxial template quality, leading to pure c-axis oriented YBCO films with enhanced crystallinity and reduced high-angle grain boundaries.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintaining excellent biaxial texture of LMO buffer layer (Δφ~7°, Δω~2.5°) throughout oxygen annealing process without grain coarsening or recrystallization.
strategies.tuning effects: Preserves high-quality epitaxial template for YBCO growth, ensuring continuous c-axis alignment and minimizing tilt defects.

strategies.tuning strategies: Relieving interfacial stress between LMO and YBCO by matching lattice constants through oxygen annealing, reducing thermal and lattice mismatch-induced defects.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables defect-free epitaxial layer-by-layer growth of YBCO, enhancing superconducting current transport capability.

strategies.tuning strategies: Suppressing formation of a-axis oriented grains in YBCO by optimizing LMO lattice parameter, which eliminates detrimental grain boundaries that obstruct supercurrent flow.
strategies.tuning effects: Achieves highly pure c-axis oriented YBCO films with improved grain connectivity, resulting in 19–26% increase in critical current (518–576 A/12 mm at 77 K self-field).

ExperimentTech.description: The study employs roll-to-roll continuous deposition for multilayer buffer stack (Al2O3/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/Epi-MgO/LMO) on Hastelloy substrates. LMO buffer layers are deposited by DC reactive magnetron sputtering and subsequently post-annealed in controlled oxygen atmosphere. YBCO superconducting layers are fabricated via low-fluorine metal-organic deposition (MOD). Characterization includes XRD for lattice constant/texture analysis, Raman spectroscopy for Mn–O vibrational modes, AFM for surface roughness, and critical current measurement using magnetic induction method.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Roll-to-roll DC reactive magnetron sputtering for LMO; low-fluorine MOD for YBCO; oxygen atmosphere post-annealing (500–620 °C, 0–2 h)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: XRD θ–2θ/ω/φ scans; Raman spectroscopy (500–650 cm⁻¹ Mn–O modes); AFM (5×5 µm² RMS roughness)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Critical current measurement at 77 K self-field using Mcorder magnetic induction system; field-dependent Jc and pinning force density (Fp) at 30–77 K

Application.description: The optimized LMO buffer layer enables high-performance second-generation high-temperature superconducting (2G-HTS) tapes for power transmission and high-field magnet applications. The 20% enhancement in critical current (518 A/12 mm at 77 K self-field) and successful 60-meter tape demonstration (576 A) validate industrial scalability.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-current power transmission cables and high-field superconducting magnets
Application.ApplicationIndex: Critical current Ic = 518 A/12 mm (77 K, self-field) for 1-meter tape; 576 A/12 mm for 60-meter tape; Jc enhancement ~20% via lattice mismatch reduction to 0.06%

MaterialSystem.description: YBa2Cu3O7−δ (Y123) single-domain bulks with embedded Y2BaCuO5 (Y211) nanoparticles; lattice parameter a ≈ b ≈ 3.82 Å, c ≈ 11.68 Å.  The material exhibits a-b plane epitaxial texture induced by SmBCO seed, reduced porosity and absence of macro-cracks in combined-modified precursor (C-MPP) samples compared to conventional (CPP) or modified (MPP) powders.
MaterialSystem.dopants: 1 wt % CeO2 (to suppress Y211 coarsening); Y211 nanoparticles (35 mol % in CPP, in-situ formed in MPP); Yb2O3 (substrate layer to block stray grains)

TunningMethod.description: A layered precursor strategy (C-MPP) that superposes conventional Y123+Y211 powder (CPP) above Y2O3+Ba2Cu3Ox powder (MPP).  During melt-growth the Y211 nanoparticles nucleate predominantly in the lower MPP layer while capillary-driven solute infiltration enriches the upper CPP layer with additional nanoscale Y211, simultaneously reducing oxygen porosity and macro-crack density.  The approach balances superconducting performance (high Jc, high levitation force) with mechanical integrity required for Maglev service.

strategies.tuning strategies: Stacking CPP (Y123+35 mol % Y211) over MPP (Y200+Y023) creates a compositional gradient that supplies extra Y211 nanoparticles to the growth front while the upper CPP layer buffers corrosive Ba–Cu–O liquid away from the seed.
strategies.tuning effects: Increases Y211/Y123 interface area → stronger flux pinning; lowers overall porosity from 25.1 % (MPP) to 18.1 % (C-MPP); eliminates 0.6 mm macro-cracks observed in MPP.

strategies.tuning strategies: Inserting a 6 mm-diameter CPP buffer pellet between SmBCO seed and main precursor prevents liquid-phase corrosion of the seed and ensures reliable epitaxial growth across the layered assembly.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables use of recyclable crystal seeds instead of fragile film seeds; maintains single-domain growth with four facet lines and no parasitic grains.

strategies.tuning strategies: Top-seeded melt-growth with identical thermal schedule for all samples guarantees uniform a-b plane alignment; the layered powder does not disturb the seeded orientation but refines Y211 distribution within the textured matrix.
strategies.tuning effects: Comparable epitaxial texture in C-MPP and CPP; reduced shrinkage (30.2 % vs 35.3 % for MPP) leading to better dimensional tolerance for batch production.

strategies.tuning strategies: CPP layer possesses higher green strength and lower melt viscosity than MPP, counteracting the thermal expansion mismatch and internal oxygen pressure that generate tensile stress and central bulging in MPP.
strategies.tuning effects: Flatter top surface, absence of 0.6 mm transverse cracks; improved shear resistance along a-b plane critical for dynamic Maglev loads.

strategies.tuning strategies: Finer, homogeneously dispersed Y211 nanoparticles (20–260 nm) generated in-situ in MPP layer and infiltrated into CPP layer reduce effective grain-boundary weak-links by increasing pinning-site density without disrupting Y123 matrix continuity.
strategies.tuning effects: Lower magnetic relaxation rate (13.0 % vs 13.9 % for CPP) indicating stronger pinning; 5 % higher force-volume density (Fv) than CPP while retaining mechanical robustness.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were fabricated by dual-powder stacking + top-seeded melt-growth (TSMG) in a single furnace run to ensure identical thermal history.  Microstructure was quantified by optical microscopy and ImageJ porosity analysis on a–c cross-sections.  Levitation force loops and 3-min relaxation were measured at 77 K using a custom SCML-05 platform above a Halbach NdFeB guideway (0.67 T at 5 mm gap).  Finite-element electromagnetic simulations (COMSOL, H-formulation) established linear normalization ranges for thickness (9–10 mm) and a-b area (441–676 mm²) to compare bulks of different sizes.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Dual-layer powder stacking + top-seeded melt-growth (TSMG); same-furnace batch processing; oxygen annealing 450 °C 220 h
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Optical microscopy; quantitative porosity analysis (ImageJ); geometric dimension mapping
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Liquid-nitrogen levitation-force loop & relaxation (SCML-05); finite-element force normalization (COMSOL Multiphysics)

Application.description: High-temperature superconducting pinning Maglev vehicles require bulks that deliver high levitation force and stiffness yet survive repetitive mechanical and electromagnetic loads.  C-MPP bulks provide 5 % higher force-volume density and lower relaxation than conventional CPP while eliminating macro-cracks and reducing porosity, translating into higher load capacity, safer hover margin and improved reliability at high speed.
Application.ApplicationScenario: HTS pinning Maglev transit systems
Application.ApplicationIndex: Levitation force density Fv ≈ 1.27e-2 N mm-3; magnetic relaxation rate R ≤ 13 %; zero-field-cooled maximum levitation force ≥ 76 N (normalized to 550 mm² × 9.5 mm)

MaterialSystem.description: The composite superconductor is based on YBa2Cu3O7-x (Y-123) matrix in which 20 wt % of Y is randomly substituted by a ternary mixture of Nd, Sm and Gd, yielding (Y,NSG)BCO unit cells. Rietveld refinement gives lattice parameters a = 3.824(2) Å, b = 3.888(9) Å, c = 11.694(0) Å, close to standard Y-123. Uniformly embedded micron-sized (Y/RE)-211 precipitates (0–2 µm) and 0.5 wt % WO3 nanoparticles (2–6 nm) create a dense network of stacking faults and local δκ fluctuations that act as strong pinning centres. A sharp (103) texture is developed by NdBCO-film seeding during infiltration growth.

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic optimisation is achieved by (i) sol-casting uniform dispersion of RE-211 and WO3 nano-inclusions, (ii) mixed-rare-earth substitution to create compositional disorder and local δκ pinning, (iii) excess-Ba processing in air to suppress RE/Ba solid solutions and porosity, (iv) net-shape gelcasting into rapid-prototyped moulds for dense, void-free green bodies, and (v) seeded infiltration growth to impose single-grain (103) texture. Together these actions maintain Jc ≈ 4 kA cm-2 at 77 K, 0 T and ≈ 0.4 kA cm-2 at 77 K, 8.5 T, while Fp peaks at 7–8 T for 10–77 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Random substitution of 20 % Y by Nd/Sm/Gd introduces local lattice-parameter mismatch and stacking faults, generating δκ-type pinning centres without lowering Tc.
strategies.tuning effects: Jc remains field-independent up to 8.5 T; Fp,max ≈ 40 N cm-3 at 77 K and 2.9e3 N cm-3 at 10 K with Bp ≈ 7–8 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Sol-casting ensures nano-WO3 (2–6 nm) and micron RE-211 particles are uniformly dispersed, creating high-density interfaces that act as point and surface pinning sites.
strategies.tuning effects: Secondary low-field Fp peak (≈ 3 T at 10 K, 0.2 T at 77 K) appears; overall pinning force density extends to 9 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: NdBCO thin-film seeds on top and bottom of the infiltrated preform impose single-grain (103) orientation during slow-cooled infiltration growth.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates weak-link grain boundaries; Jc(0) = 4.4 kA cm-2 at 77 K exceeds literature values for stacked cylinders.

strategies.tuning strategies: Excess 2 wt % Ba suppresses RE/Ba solid-solution formation and spherical porosity, reducing internal tensile stress and maintaining dense microstructure.
strategies.tuning effects: Void-free matrix with 37 % uniform RE-211 content; sharp ΔTc = 1.5 K indicates excellent inter-grain connectivity.

strategies.tuning strategies: Infiltration growth converts polycrystalline preform into a single-grain cylinder, removing high-angle boundaries that limit current percolation.
strategies.tuning effects: Magnetic shielding demonstrated at 41 G (dc) at 77 K; levitation of 15 g SmCo5 magnet achieved.

ExperimentTech.description: Fabrication combines rapid-prototyped gelcasting (RPGC) for net-shape green bodies with seeded infiltration growth (IG) to obtain dense, textured cylinders. Characterisation includes XRD (Rietveld), optical/FE-SEM, EDAX, and AC-susceptibility. Property evaluation employs vibrating-sample magnetometry up to 9 T (10–77 K) to extract Jc via extended Bean model and Fp scaling analysis.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Rapid-prototyped gelcasting (RPGC) of sol-cast slurry + seeded infiltration growth (IG)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (Rietveld), optical microscopy, FE-SEM, EDAX, AC-susceptometry
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: VSM magnetisation hysteresis (±9 T, 10–77 K), homemade solenoid shielding test

Application.description: The monolithic hollow cylinder delivers high in-field Jc and strong magnetic shielding at liquid-nitrogen temperature, enabling compact, cryogen-free magnetic shields or trapped-field devices without mechanical stacking.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Liquid-nitrogen-operated magnetic shielding tubes and compact superconducting solenoids/magnets
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(77 K, 0 T) = 4.4 kA cm-2; Jc(77 K, 8.5 T) = 0.4 kA cm-2; Fp,max(77 K) = 39.6 N cm-3; shielding ≥ 41 G at 77 K

MaterialSystem.description: GdBa2Cu3O7-δ (Gd123) orthorhombic single-grain matrix with embedded Gd2BaCuO5 (Gd211) non-superconducting particles; Ag2O added to reduce micro-cracking; nanosize BaCeO3 (perovskite) homogeneously dispersed, acting as Ce source that segregates on Gd211 surfaces and suppresses Ostwald ripening, leading to refined Gd211 and possible Ba/Gd substitution point defects.
MaterialSystem.dopants: nanosize BaCeO3 (0.189–2.836 wt%, equivalent 0.1–1.5 wt% CeO2)

TunningMethod.description: Nanosize BaCeO3 is dissolved in the peritectic melt during TSMG, releasing Ce4+ that adsorbs on Gd211 surfaces to inhibit coarsening (refinement) and simultaneously modifies melt chemistry to tune Ba/Gd substitution level; the synergistic control of Gd211 size/distribution and chemical pinning density optimizes Jc and trapped field.

strategies.tuning strategies: Add nanosize BaCeO3 to supply Ce4+ in the melt; Ce segregates on Gd211 surfaces and suppresses Ostwald ripening, yielding finer Gd211 particles that provide stronger flux pinning.
strategies.tuning effects: Gd211 size decreases monotonically with BaCeO3 content; V211/d211 ratio rises, enhancing zero-field Jc and trapped field.

strategies.tuning strategies: Dissolved Ce and Ba from BaCeO3 alter Ba/Gd substitution level in Gd123 lattice, creating point-defect (chemical) pinning centres; excess Ce reduces Tc while optimal level maximizes secondary peak in Jc-B.
strategies.tuning effects: Non-monotonic Tc and Jc(B) behaviour; secondary peak shifts to lower B as substitution decreases, enabling high in-field Jc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Refined Gd211 particles improve interfacial area between superconducting matrix and insulating inclusions, increasing pinning site density without blocking current paths.
strategies.tuning effects: Higher volume fraction of nanometre-scale interfaces raises bulk pinning force and critical current density.

strategies.tuning strategies: Single-grain growth ensured by TSMG with NdBCO seed; BaCeO3 addition does not trigger parasitic grains, maintaining clean, low-angle domain boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates weak-link grain boundaries, preserving high inter-grain Jc and conical trapped-field profile.

strategies.tuning strategies: Ag2O addition and fine Gd211 dispersion reduce thermal-expansion mismatch stresses; total pushing of Gd211 in high-BaCeO3 samples creates local stress-free zones.
strategies.tuning effects: Minimises macro-cracking, allowing full 17.5 mm diameter single-grain bulks to survive magnetisation cycles.

ExperimentTech.description: TSMG with sol-gel nanosize BaCeO3 enables homogeneous Ce distribution; polarised-light microscopy, SEM-EDS and image analysis quantify Gd211 size/volume; XRD confirms single 00l orientation; VSM-ZFC gives Tc and transition width; vibrating-sample magnetometry with extended Bean model delivers Jc-B at 77 K; Hall-scan mapping yields 3D trapped-field profiles after 1.4 T field-cooling.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Top-Seeded Melt-Growth (TSMG) with sol-gel nanosize BaCeO3 addition, oxygen annealing 400 °C 10 d
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: XRD (θ–2θ), optical polarised microscopy, SEM + EDS, image-processing particle analysis
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: VSM zero-field-cooling Tc, extended-Bean Jc from M-B loops at 77 K, Hall-probe trapped-field mapping at 77 K

Application.description: Bulk single-grain GdBCO-Ag superconductors are targeted as high-field trapped-flux permanent magnets for compact motors, magnetic bearings and NMR/MRI insert coils; high Jc and large trapped field at 77 K are key performance metrics.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Superconducting permanent magnets / trapped-flux devices operating at liquid-nitrogen temperature
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc0 ≈ 6e4 A cm-2 at 77 K, 0 T; maximum trapped field ≈ 0.42 T at 77 K for 17.5 mm diameter sample

MaterialSystem.description: REBCO (REBa2Cu3O7-δ, RE = Y0.5Gd0.5) superconducting film with dense BaZrO3 columnar defects (~1.1e11 cm-2, 5–9 nm diameter, continuous along c-axis) embedded in a 1.5 µm-thick layer; no secondary phases or agglomerates observed, yielding strong c-axis texture and high pinning density.

TunningMethod.description: High-density BaZrO3 columnar defects are introduced by MOCVD to create strong δl-pinning centers; the coexistence of δTc-pinning is evidenced by GIS analysis, giving a hybrid pinning landscape that enlarges the elastic vortex-glass region and suppresses relaxation rates below 6 % up to 8 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Incorporate 10 % BaZrO3 into REBCO matrix to form insulating columnar defects that act as strong core-pinning sites, shifting the dominant pinning mechanism from δTc to δl with increasing field.
strategies.tuning effects: Raises irreversibility field and lift factor (~20 at 4.2 K, self-field), extends high-Js region to high temperature and high magnetic field.

strategies.tuning strategies: Grow continuous BaZrO3 nano-columns along c-axis via MOCVD, ensuring coherent interface with REBCO matrix and minimizing weak-link grain boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Provides aligned 1-D pinning corridors, reduces vortex creep, and maintains Js > 15 MA cm-2 at 3 K, self-field.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain sharp c-axis texture during MOCVD growth so that columnar defects are parallel to the vortex lines, maximizing pinning efficiency.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates second magnetization peak and preserves symmetric MHLs, indicating bulk pinning dominance and uniform current flow.

strategies.tuning strategies: Control lattice mismatch between BaZrO3 and REBCO to keep residual strain low, preventing crack formation in the 1.5 µm film.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables defect columns to remain continuous over hundreds of nanometres, sustaining high pinning density without film degradation.

strategies.tuning strategies: Suppress high-angle grain boundaries by epitaxial growth on single-crystal-like template, reducing weak-link losses.
strategies.tuning effects: Keeps superconducting transition width narrow enough to preserve high pinning energy Uc ≈ 145 K up to 7.5 T.

ExperimentTech.description: MOCVD fabricates 1.5 µm-thick REBCO films with 10 % BaZrO3; STEM visualizes columnar defect morphology; VSM-PPMS performs dynamic magnetization-relaxation (sweep rates 50–200 Oe s-1) to extract Q, Js, and construct vortex phase diagram; Bean model and GIS analysis distinguish δl vs δTc pinning.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Dynamic magnetization-relaxation (Q = dlnJs/dln(dB/dt)), Bean critical-state model, GIS pinning-function analysis

Application.description: High-temperature, high-field coated conductors for compact fusion magnets and MRI systems require retention of several MA cm-2 current density at 77 K and above 3 T; present films deliver Js ~ several 0.1 MA cm-2 at t = 0.76 and 3–8 T, with relaxation < 6 %, indicating strong potential after further δTc-pinning enhancement.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Fusion reactor high-field magnets and high-performance MRI inserts
Application.ApplicationIndex: Js > 15 MA cm-2 (3 K, self-field), lift factor ~20 (4.2 K), Uc/kB ≈ 145 K (7.5 T), relaxation rate Q < 0.06 (T < 50 K, μ0H ≤ 8 T)

MaterialSystem.description: EuBa2Cu3O7-x (EuBCO) coated conductors on Hastelloy substrate with IBAD/PLD buffer stack; c-axis oriented (00l) texture preserved after etching; slight oxygen deficiency (δ↑, c-axis lattice constant ↑) and minor BaCuO2 phase detected after prolonged FeCl3 attack.

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic optimization of FeCl3 wet-etch parameters (concentration, temperature, time) to remove 25 µm Cu stabilizer while suppressing superconducting-layer delamination and oxygen loss, thereby retaining Ic and n-value.

strategies.tuning strategies: Set FeCl3 concentration at 200 g L⁻¹ to balance etch rate and chemical attack; lower concentrations prolong exposure and increase oxygen loss, whereas higher concentrations accelerate side-reaction with Ag and REBCO, forming BaCuO2 and amorphous Cu–Ba phases.
strategies.tuning effects: Ic retention peaks at 92 % (vs 77 % at 50 g L⁻¹ and 71 % at 300 g L⁻¹); n-value maximized to 29.

strategies.tuning strategies: Lower bath temperature to 0 °C to slow Fe³⁺ diffusion through intrinsic pinholes in the 2.8 µm Ag cap, reducing under-cut erosion at Ag/REBCO interface and preventing local delamination.
strategies.tuning effects: Ic retention rises to 98 % and n-value to 33.7; SEM shows intact interface without edge peeling.

strategies.tuning strategies: Minimize immersion time to ~17 min (just complete Cu removal) to limit post-Cu chemical attack on the exposed Ag surface and subsequent oxygen out-diffusion from REBCO lattice.
strategies.tuning effects: Extending time to 30 min drops Ic retention to 82 % and n-value to 27.2; XRD I(005)/I(006) ↑ and Raman O(4) softening confirm increased oxygen vacancies.

strategies.tuning strategies: Avoid over-etch that generates ring-like cracks around native defects; optimized parameters keep crack diameter ≤10 µm and suppress inter-grain delamination, maintaining percolative current path.
strategies.tuning effects: Micro-cracks density minimized, preserving long-range connectivity and high n-value >25 required for persistent-current-mode magnets.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use low-temperature (0 °C) etch to reduce thermal-expansion mismatch stress during rapid Cu dissolution, preventing buckling of thin REBCO film on flexible substrate.
strategies.tuning effects: No observable buckling or wrinkle formation; c-axis lattice constant increase limited to <0.02 Å, keeping residual stress low.

ExperimentTech.description: Sequential wet etching (FeCl3 for Cu; NH₃·H₂O/H₂O₂ for Ag) followed by multi-scale characterization to correlate etch parameters with superconducting degradation.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: FeCl3 aqueous etching (0–300 g L⁻¹, 0–60 °C, 10–30 min); NH₃·H₂O/H₂O₂ (1:4) silver cap removal at 5 °C.
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: SEM/EDS for surface delamination; XRD θ–2θ for phase purity, c-axis lattice constant, I(005)/I(006) oxygen indicator; Raman (488 nm) for O(4) phonon shift and oxygen vacancy quantification.
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe Ic (77 K, self-field, 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion) and n-value extraction from E–I curves.

Application.description: Enable superconducting joints for kilometer-scale REBCO magnets operating in persistent-current mode with minimal Ic penalty.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Superconducting joints for NMR, fusion magnets and SMES coils fabricated from REBCO coated conductors.
Application.ApplicationIndex: Ic retention ≥95 %, n-value ≥25 after Cu removal over 10 mm joint length.

MaterialSystem.description: YBa2Cu3O6+x (YBCO) thin films (~200 nm) grown epitaxially on 10 mm × 10 mm SrTiO3 (100) single-crystal substrates; APC-free reference and 4 wt % BaZrO3 (BZO)-doped variants. BZO self-assembles into ~6 nm diameter c-axis-aligned nanorods (spacing ≈ 20 nm) that act as columnar artificial pinning centres, slightly reducing the electron mean-free path and lowering Jc,0 while strongly enhancing in-field Jc(B) and accommodation field B*.

TunningMethod.description: By introducing coherent BZO nanorod defects the authors simultaneously tailor flux-pinning strength, current-carrying capability and quench energetics. The nanorods raise B*, flatten Jc(B), lower the minimum quench energy (MQE) and accelerate normal-zone propagation velocity (NZPV) at high T/B, offering a single compositional route to trade-off stability against detectability.

strategies.tuning strategies: Incorporation of 4 wt % BaZrO3 into YBCO matrix to create dense, c-axis-oriented nanorod defects that serve as strong artificial pinning centres.
strategies.tuning effects: Increases accommodation field B* and in-field Jc(B), but reduces zero-field Jc,0 due to shortened electron mean-free path; lowers MQE and raises NZPV at high T/B because pinning localises thermally activated flux flow (TAFF) and heat dissipation.

strategies.tuning strategies: Epitaxial deposition on lattice-matched STO (100) substrate ensures high-quality YBCO/BZO interface and coherent nanorod formation without secondary phases.
strategies.tuning effects: Minimises interfacial disorder, preserves high Tc, and enables uniform nanorod alignment for optimal vortex pinning along the c-axis.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploits slight lattice mismatch between BZO nanorods and YBCO matrix to generate local strain fields around each defect.
strategies.tuning effects: Strain fields further enhance pinning potential, contributing to the observed increase in B* and reduced MQE by localising vortex motion.

strategies.tuning strategies: Patterning 50 µm-wide microbridges by maskless photolithography and wet etching to eliminate extrinsic grain boundaries and create well-defined current paths.
strategies.tuning effects: Removes weak-link limitations, allowing intrinsic pinning properties of BZO nanorods to dominate transport and quench behaviour.

strategies.tuning strategies: PLD growth conditions optimised to maintain sharp c-axis texture of YBCO while accommodating embedded BZO nanorods.
strategies.tuning effects: Ensures correlated pinning along the field direction, maximising Jc(B) and producing the observed factor-of-two NZPV increase at high temperature.

ExperimentTech.description: Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) prepared 200 nm films; patterning by maskless photolithography + H3PO4 wet etch. Critical current density extracted from 10 K magnetic hysteresis loops using Bean model. Quench dynamics measured in PPMS (20–70 K, 0–8 T) with NI PXIe-1073 data acquisition; 0.7 s heat pulses generated by on-chip 220 Ω resistor. NZPV determined from 10 mV threshold crossing time between two voltage taps 1 mm apart. TEM confirmed ~6 nm BZO nanorods.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD); maskless photolithography; wet chemical etching (H3PO4)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: SQUID-VSM magnetic hysteresis (Bean model Jc); Cs-corrected STEM (200 kV, HAADF); I–V transport (1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: PPMS + NI PXIe-1073 quench setup; time-resolved voltage traces; MQE ≈ I²Rt; NZPV from 10 mV threshold delay

Application.description: Understanding and optimising quench behaviour is essential for protecting high-field HTS magnets used in fusion, accelerators and MRI. Faster NZPV and lower MQE in BZO-doped YBCO improve detectability but reduce stability margin; results guide design of quench-detection systems and stabiliser architectures for next-generation REBCO magnets.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field HTS magnets (fusion reactors, particle accelerators, advanced MRI) requiring reliable quench detection and protection.
Application.ApplicationIndex: In-field Jc(10 K, 8 T) ≈ 2e10 A m⁻² for BZO-doped vs ~5e9 A m⁻² APC-free; NZPV up to 200 mm s⁻¹ at 70 K, 0.9 Ic; MQE ≈ 0.1–1 J, ~50 % lower in BZO-doped at low T.

MaterialSystem.description: GdBCO (GdBa2Cu3Oy) REBCO superconducting films grown on IBAD tapes with CeO2 buffer; BaHfO3 (BHO) perovskite nanoparticles (1.6–2.2 nm in solution, 2–10 nm in film) are dispersed as artificial pinning centers. Films exhibit sharp biaxial texture (Δϕ ≈ 2–3°) independent of the 7.5° buffer Δϕ, indicating self-epitaxial growth and low-angle grain boundaries favorable for high Jc.

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic optimization: (i) BHO nanoparticle content tunes flux-pinning strength; (ii) repeated coating/crystallization increases thickness without Ic degradation; (iii) self-epitaxial growth on fine-grained IBAD templates sharpens REBCO texture; (iv) low oxygen partial pressure during crystallization minimizes BaCO3 residues; (v) thermal budget controls nanoparticle coarsening and strain.

strategies.tuning strategies: Graded addition of 0–3.4 mol % BHO nanoparticles creates high-density APCs; higher BHO raises low-field Jc but slightly suppresses Tc (~1 K) via lattice strain/oxygen deficiency.
strategies.tuning effects: 171 A/4-mm-w at 20 K, 18 T (3.1 µm, 2.7 mol % BHO); extrapolated 162 A/4-mm-w at 20 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Self-epitaxial growth during FF-MOD crystallization on IBAD templates reduces REBCO Δϕ from 7.5° (CeO2) to 2–3° within 0.35 µm, independent of buffer misalignment up to ~8.5°.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables >500 A/4-mm-w at 77 K, s.f. even on 7.5°-misaligned buffers; maintains high Jc up to 3 µm thickness.

strategies.tuning strategies: 100–700 nm RF-sputtered CeO2 surface modification on IBAD tape provides chemically compatible, smooth growth front; multi-cycle coating/crystallization yields clean interfaces between sub-layers.
strategies.tuning effects: Flat surface morphology (SEM), no precipitates, uniform BHO dispersion (TEM/EDX); supports repeated coating without Jc degradation.

strategies.tuning strategies: Low-angle grain boundaries (Δϕ ≤ 3°) achieved via self-epitaxy minimize weak-link behavior; BHO nanoparticles located intragranularly avoid grain-boundary blocking.
strategies.tuning effects: Linear Ic vs thickness up to 3 µm; high Jc maintained in thick films.

strategies.tuning strategies: Controlled oxygenation at 200–500 °C relieves lattice strain induced by BHO incorporation; low-temperature crystallization (800–840 °C) limits thermal mismatch with metal substrate.
strategies.tuning effects: Prevents film cracking in 200-m-long tapes; uniform Ic distribution (467 A/4-mm-w average at 77 K).

ExperimentTech.description: FF-MOD (fluorine-free metal-organic decomposition) reel-to-reel slot-die coating on IBAD tapes; multi-pass coating/pyrolysis/crystallization for thickness scaling. Characterization by XRD (Δϕ), SEM, cross-sectional TEM/EDX for nanoparticle distribution. Ic measured DC four-probe (1 µV/cm) in self-field and up to 18 T, angular Ic up to 8 T, longitudinal Ic mapping with THEVA Tapestar.

ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: DC four-probe critical current (self-field, 18 T, 8 T angular), THEVA Tapestar longitudinal mapping

Application.description: Low-cost, high-field magnets for NMR, accelerators and fusion reactors demand high Ic at 20–77 K under ≥20 T. FF-MOD REBCO tapes deliver competitive performance without expensive PLD hardware.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field accelerator and fusion magnets, compact NMR inserts
Application.ApplicationIndex: Ic = 171 A/4-mm-w at 20 K, 18 T; extrapolated 162 A/4-mm-w at 20 K, 20 T; 467 A/4-mm-w at 77 K, s.f. over 200 m length

MaterialSystem.description: Epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7-x (YBCO) films (~250 nm) on (001) SrTiO3 single crystals. Lattice parameters: a(YBCO)=3.87 Å, a(BYNTO)=4.27 Å, a(ZrO2)=5.09 Å. Films contain self-assembled Ba2Y(Nb/Ta)O6 (BYNTO) nanocolumns (5–16 nm Ø) and extrinsic ZrO2 nanoislands (45 nm Ø, 25 nm height) coated by a thin BaZrO3 layer (~0.4 % mismatch) that triggers dense stacking faults (~2×10^4 µm^-2) and Y248 intergrowths. Excellent out-of-plane texture (FWHM 0.15°) is preserved despite high defect density.

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic flux-pinning enhancement is achieved by simultaneously introducing two distinct artificial pinning centres: (i) substrate-surface decoration with polymer-assisted-deposited ZrO2 nanoislands that generate high-density stacking faults and (ii) in-situ self-assembly of BYNTO nanocolumns via composite-target PLD. The cooperative defect landscape eliminates temperature scaling of the pinning force and activates multiple pinning channels, especially above 5 T and below 50 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Co-deposit 2.5 at.% Ba2YNbO6 + 2.5 at.% Ba2YTaO6 through a composite PLD target to form randomly distributed yet c-axis-oriented BYNTO nanocolumns that act as strong correlated pinning centres over a wide field range.
strategies.tuning effects: Nanocolumns provide continuous 1D pinning paths, raising Jc at intermediate fields; their diameter (5–16 nm) and meandering character optimise the matching field without severely depressing Tc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Pre-decorate the SrTiO3 substrate with PAD-synthesised ZrO2 nanoislands (375 µm^-2, 20 % coverage) to create heterogeneous nucleation sites that locally disrupt YBCO growth and seed dense stacking faults and Y248 intergrowths.
strategies.tuning effects: Generates abundant planar defects parallel to the ab-plane that act as isotropic high-field pins, improving Jc above 5 T and below 50 K while avoiding additional nanocolumn nucleation at the interface.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit lattice mismatch (16 %) between cubic ZrO2 and BYNTO to first form a thin compliant BaZrO3 interlayer, relaxing interfacial strain and enabling subsequent defect accommodation through misfit dislocations and stacking faults.
strategies.tuning effects: Local strain fields surrounding each nanoisland nucleate partial dislocations and stacking faults, creating strong point-like and planar pinning sites effective at high magnetic fields.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain high-temperature epitaxial PLD at 840 °C and 1.8 nm s^-1 on (001) STO to preserve sharp biaxial texture (FWHM 0.15°) despite high nanoparticle and defect densities.
strategies.tuning effects: Excellent crystalline alignment minimises weak-link grain boundaries, ensuring that added defects enhance pinning without introducing current-blocking high-angle boundaries.

strategies.tuning strategies: Combine both nanocolumnar (BYNTO) and nanoparticle (ZrO2-derived) pinning architectures in a single film, producing a multi-modal defect distribution that covers a broader range of vortex sizes and field orientations.
strategies.tuning effects: Absence of Fp(T,H) scaling evidences concurrent pinning mechanisms; stacking faults dominate at low-T/high-field while nanocolumns prevail at intermediate fields, yielding higher Jc above 9 T than either defect type alone.

ExperimentTech.description: Polymer-assisted deposition (PAD) was employed for cost-effective, water-based synthesis of ZrO2 nanoparticles subsequently transferred as nanoislands onto SrTiO3. Epitaxial YBCO-BYNTO films were grown by pulsed-laser deposition using a KrF laser. Microstructure was analysed by AFM, XRD rocking curves, and cross-sectional HAADF-STEM coupled with EDX. DC four-probe transport measurements in 4.2–77 K, 0–18 T provided Jc(H) and Fp(H) with 1 µV cm^-1 criterion.
