ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Atomic force microscopy; X-ray diffraction (rocking curves); High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy; Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: DC in-field critical current density versus temperature (4.2–77 K) and magnetic field (0–18 T) with 1 µV cm^-1 electric-field criterion

Application.description: High-field (>12 T) superconducting magnets for fusion reactors, high-energy physics accelerators and low-temperature (4.2–50 K) MRI/NMR systems require coated conductors that maintain high critical current densities. The demonstrated synergistic pinning raises Jc at 18 T and 4.2 K relative to conventional nanocolumn-only films, offering a route towards >20 T REBCO insert coils.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Fusion magnets, accelerator dipoles, high-field MRI/NMR inserts operating at 4.2–50 K and above 9 T
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(4.2 K, 18 T) ≈ 2.4× that of nanocolumn-only film; irreversibility field >9 T below 50 K; Fp non-scaling evidences enhanced high-field pinning channel

MaterialSystem.description: REBCO (REBa2Cu3O7-δ, RE = Y, Eu) coated conductors deposited on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy C-276 substrates with LaMnO3 cap. EuBCO layer additionally contains 3.5 mol% BaHfO3 (BHO) nanorod APCs. In-plane texture Δφ ≈ 6–7° (LMO 200 φ-scan).

TunningMethod.description: Angular anisotropy of Jc is mitigated by face-to-face double-stacked (FFDS) architecture that electrically parallels two REBCO tapes with complementary Ic-B-θ profiles (YBCO strong at B//ab, EuBCO+BHO strong at B//c). Low-resistance solder interface (~2 nΩ cm²) enables current sharing so the stack Ic equals the sum of individual tapes and the minimum Ic is lifted.

strategies.tuning strategies: Introduce BaHfO3 nanorod APCs into EuBCO layer to create strong correlated pinning for B//c-axis, selectively enhancing Jc at field angles where YBCO is weak.
strategies.tuning effects: EuBCO+BHO tape shows higher Jc at θ = 0° (B//c) than pure YBCO, providing complementary angular dependence.

strategies.tuning strategies: Join YBCO and EuBCO+BHO tapes face-to-face with 2–4 µm Sn63Pb37 solder layer to obtain low interfacial resistance (~2 nΩ cm²) enabling efficient current redistribution.
strategies.tuning effects: Excess current transfers from the first-quenched tape to the partner tape, so stack Ic ≈ Ic,YBCO + Ic,EuBCO and overall anisotropy is reduced.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain high in-plane texture (Δφ ≈ 6–7°) in both YBCO and EuBCO layers via IBAD-MgO/LMO template to ensure strong ab-plane Jc and minimize weak-link grain boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: High texture preserves intrinsically high Jc at B//ab (θ = 90°) so the complementary addition of BHO-doped tape mainly boosts B//c performance without degrading ab-plane performance.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use reel-to-reel soldering at 200 °C to laminate tapes; thin solder layer accommodates thermal-expansion mismatch and avoids cracking, keeping residual strain low.
strategies.tuning effects: Mechanical integrity is retained while providing a uniform, low-resistance bonding interface for stable current sharing under Lorentz force.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ PLD growth conditions that yield dense, epitaxial films with low-angle boundaries; BHO nanorods further interrupt continuous grain-boundary paths, reducing weak-link sensitivity.
strategies.tuning effects: Improved inter-granular connectivity raises the minimum Jc across all angles and supports higher overall stack current.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples prepared by reel-to-reel PLD on IBAD-MgO substrates followed by reel-to-reel Sn63Pb37 soldering to assemble FFDS conductors. Texture quantified by X-ray pole-figure/φ-scan. I-V curves measured with 4-probe transport at 65 K, 1.5 T while rotating field from −40° to 220°. Equivalent-circuit model incorporating percolation-transition Rsc and constant Rc fitted to extract interface resistance.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD); reel-to-reel Sn63Pb37 soldering (200 °C)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray pole-figure & φ-scan texture analysis
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: 4-probe transport I-V at variable angle (65 K, 1.5 T); equivalent-circuit modelling

Application.description: High-field magnets and superconducting coils require conductors with nearly isotropic Ic under changing field orientation to maximize winding pack current density and simplify quench protection. FFDS REBCO tapes deliver higher minimum Ic and lower angular standard deviation than single tapes.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field accelerator magnets, fusion magnets, compact MRI/NMR coils
Application.ApplicationIndex: Stack critical current Ic,FFDS(θ) ≈ Ic,YBCO(θ) + Ic,EuBCO+BHO(θ) at 65 K, 1.5 T; anisotropy σ(Ic)/⟨Ic⟩ reduced from 0.18 (YBCO) and 0.15 (EuBCO+BHO) to 0.07 (FFDS)

MaterialSystem.description: Epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7−δ (YBCO) thin films (c-axis oriented, 300–360 nm) were grown on MgO(100) single crystals via SrTiO3 (STO) or STO+CeO2 nanocomposite (NC) buffer layers (100–150 nm). The NC buffer self-assembles vertical CeO2 nanorods (dia. ~tens of nm, spacing 10–20 nm) inside an STO matrix, creating a dense lattice-mismatch network that injects threading dislocations (density 10–20 μm⁻¹) and local strain into the overlying YBCO without any secondary-phase addition inside the superconductor.
MaterialSystem.dopants: None inside YBCO; CeO2 nanorods reside only in the buffer layer

TunningMethod.description: Vortex pinning is strengthened by substrate-induced crystal defects rather than by artificial pinning centres within YBCO. Two synergistic levers are exploited: (i) choosing a nanocomposite (STO+CeO2) buffer that supplies a higher density of interfacial misfit and threading dislocations compared with a pure STO buffer, and (ii) tuning the YBCO deposition laser frequency (10–100 Hz) to control defect morphology—low frequency yields straight c-axis dislocations for strong correlated pinning, whereas high frequency produces wavy dislocations that weaken c-axis correlation. The combined strategy maximises the flux-pinning force density Fp especially at low temperature and high field while avoiding Tc degradation typical of secondary-phase additions.

strategies.tuning strategies: Insert an epitaxial STO+CeO2 nanocomposite buffer between MgO and YBCO; the CeO2 nanorods create abundant nanoscale STO/CeO2 interfaces that generate a high density of threading dislocations which propagate straight into YBCO and act as c-axis-correlated pinning centres.
strategies.tuning effects: Fp,max(77 K) rises to 4.13 GN m⁻³ (vs 1.56 GN m⁻³ for STO buffer) and Fp(20 K, 9 T) reaches 665 GN m⁻³, both the highest among all samples.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit lattice mismatch (STO/MgO 7.4 %, CeO2/MgO 26 %) to introduce controlled misfit strain and dislocations inside the buffer; the strain field is partially transferred into YBCO, producing nanoscale elastic strain that supplements core pinning without elongating the YBCO c-axis or suppressing Tc.
strategies.tuning effects: Buffered samples retain Tc ≈ 89 K even at 100 Hz deposition, whereas YBCO on STO single crystal drops to 86.7 K; self-field Jc(77 K) stays above 2 MA cm⁻² for NC buffer.

strategies.tuning strategies: Lower the YBCO laser repetition rate to 20 Hz to maintain straight, vertical threading dislocations; higher frequency (100 Hz) induces meandering dislocations and sub-grain misorientation that reduce the coherence of c-axis pinning.
strategies.tuning effects: Straight dislocations at 20 Hz give the strongest B||c pinning, evidenced by the highest normalised Jc at 40 K above 3 T; wavy dislocations at 100 Hz weaken c-axis correlation and lower Fp by ~30 %.

strategies.tuning strategies: Preserve cube-on-cube epitaxy of both STO and CeO2 on MgO (Δφ < 3° for STO) so that the YBCO layer inherits sharp biaxial texture; the well-aligned ab-planes minimise high-angle grain boundaries that would otherwise limit current flow.
strategies.tuning effects: Low resistivity ρ(95 K) and high self-field Jc (>2.6 MA cm⁻²) are maintained; angular Jc at 65 K shows isotropic enhancement relative to bare YBCO, indicating texture is not degraded by buffer-induced defects.

strategies.tuning strategies: Keep the YBCO layer chemically pure—no BMO or other secondary phases are added; pinning originates solely from substrate-induced defects, eliminating the Tc and self-field Jc penalties usually caused by nanorod overdoping or strain-induced oxygen disorder.
strategies.tuning effects: Compared with YBCO+5 vol% BaHfO3 nanorod film, the NC-buffered pure YBCO exhibits lower Fp at 77 K but surpasses the nanorod sample in normalised Jc above 3 T at 40 K, demonstrating competitive performance without foreign phases.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were fabricated by separate-chamber pulsed-laser deposition (KrF, λ = 248 nm) with precise frequency control. Crystal quality and epitaxy were verified by high-resolution XRD (2θ/ω and φ scans). Cross-sectional STEM coupled with EDX mapping visualised dislocation trajectories, CeO2 nanorod morphology and Y2O3 nanoparticles. Superconducting properties were measured in a PPMS using four-probe micro-bridges (50–100 μm wide) under fields up to 9 T; Jc was extracted with 1 μV cm⁻¹ criterion and angular Jc–θ curves were recorded to quantify pinning anisotropy.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) with variable laser repetition rate (10–100 Hz) for YBCO; STO and STO+CeO2 buffers deposited at 10 Hz, 880 °C, 400 mTorr O2
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (2θ/ω, φ scans, rocking curves); scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM); energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) four-probe transport under magnetic fields (0–9 T, 20–77 K); angular-dependent critical current density Jc(θ) at fixed fields

Application.description: Coated conductors for high-field magnets and cryogenic power devices require high in-field critical current at temperatures ≤ 40 K and fields ≥ 5 T. The substrate-induced pinning approach demonstrated here delivers record flux-pinning force density (665 GN m⁻³ at 20 K, 9 T) without sacrificing Tc or adding secondary phases, offering a scalable route to enhance low-temperature/high-field performance of pure YBCO tapes.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Low-temperature high-field magnets, fusion magnets, and cryogenic power cables using REBCO coated conductors
Application.ApplicationIndex: Fp(20 K, 9 T) = 665 GN m⁻³; Jc(77 K, self-field) = 2.63 MA cm⁻²; Tc ≥ 89 K

MaterialSystem.description: EuBa2Cu3O7−δ (EuBCO) high-temperature superconductor with BaHfO3 (BHO) nanocolumnar doping, deposited on C276/Al2O3/Y2O3/IBAD-MgO/LaMnO3/CeO2 buffered metal tapes. The EuBCO layer exhibits dominant c-axis orientation and contains well-aligned second-phase BHO nanocolumns for flux pinning. Localized arched grains and Cu-rich precipitates appear at tape edges due to thermal decomposition.

TunningMethod.description: Transverse Jc uniformity is optimized by mitigating temperature gradients induced by helical tape travel in reel-to-reel MPMT-PLD. Strategies focus on suppressing localized overheating at edges, controlling elemental segregation, and preventing buffer/EuBCO decomposition that creates arched weak-link grains.

strategies.tuning strategies: Suppress Cu segregation toward tape edges by homogenizing transverse temperature profile, thereby avoiding Cu-rich precipitates that reduce local Jc.
strategies.tuning effects: Left-edge Jc rises from 73 % to ~100 % of center value; Ba/Cu ratio uniformity improves.

strategies.tuning strategies: Eliminate arched non-c-axis grains generated by buffer-layer volumetric expansion; maintain low-angle grain boundaries for strong supercurrent percolation.
strategies.tuning effects: Removes weak-link paths; recovers ~27 % Jc loss at edges.

strategies.tuning strategies: Prevent partial decomposition of CeO2 cap and LaMnO3 buffer to preserve flat, epitaxial template for subsequent EuBCO growth.
strategies.tuning effects: Suppresses arched morphology; retains high in-plane texture and BHO nanocolumn alignment.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain uniform c-axis orientation across 10 mm width by minimizing transverse temperature deviation during multi-turn deposition.
strategies.tuning effects: Micro-XRD (005) peak intensity becomes uniform; edge crystallinity equals center.

strategies.tuning strategies: Reduce torsional stress and edge friction against accumulated coating residue in inter-lane gaps to avoid localized overheating and Ni contamination.
strategies.tuning effects: Prevents hot spots > epitaxial temperature; eliminates Ni transfer and associated decomposition.

ExperimentTech.description: Industrial reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn pulsed laser deposition (MPMT-PLD) fabricates hundreds-of-meters EuBCO tapes. Transverse Jc mapping is enabled by mechanical slitting into 1–2 mm filaments combined with four-probe transport and Bean-model magnetic moment measurements. Microstructural root-cause analysis employs micro-XRD (50 µm beam), SEM-EDS, and FIB-TEM to correlate arched grains, Cu segregation, and buffer decomposition with Jc degradation.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn pulsed laser deposition (MPMT-PLD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Micro-X-ray diffraction (micro-XRD), SEM-EDS, FIB-TEM with EDS, ICP-OES
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe critical current (1 µV cm−1 criterion), vibrating-sample magnetometry (Bean model), slitting-based transverse Jc profiling

Application.description: Long-length EuBCO coated conductors are required for high-field magnets, fusion reactors, and superconducting cables where uniform transverse critical current ensures stable operation and minimizes AC losses.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field REBCO magnets, compact fusion systems, superconducting power cables
Application.ApplicationIndex: Engineering critical current density Je (77 K, self-field) ≥ 2.5e9 A m−2 across 10 mm width with ≤ 5 % transverse variation

MaterialSystem.description: EuBa2Cu3O7-δ (EuBCO) matrix with 6 mol% BaHfO3 (BHO) dopant; c-axis lattice parameter ≈ 11.73 Å; c-axis-oriented grains with some a-axis grains in thick layers; highly splayed BHO nanocolumns (0–20° tilt) and nanoparticles; misoriented EuBCO grains nucleated on Cu-O particles; random BHO-free layered regions; good in-plane (FWHM φ-scan ≈ 2°) and out-of-plane (FWHM ω-scan ≈ 1.5°) texture.

TunningMethod.description: Thickness-dependent microstructure evolution is exploited to tune flux-pinning landscapes: multi-cycle ultra-fast PLD increases BHO splay angle and generates natural defects, while misoriented grains are tolerated to trade-off self-field Jc for superior in-field and angular performance.

strategies.tuning strategies: 6 mol% BHO doping introduces dense nanocolumns/nanoparticles that act as correlated and random pinning centers; splay angle increases with thickness, creating a 3-D pinning web.
strategies.tuning effects: Jc(B) decay slows at 4.2 K, yielding ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 14 T; Jc(θ) anisotropy reduced at 30 K, 5 T.

strategies.tuning strategies: Accept limited misoriented EuBCO grains grown on Cu-O particles; their low-angle boundaries do not severely suppress Tc but create additional isotropic pinning sites.
strategies.tuning effects: Slightly lower self-field Jc (1.4 vs 2.6 MA/cm² at 77 K) but higher irreversibility field and isotropic Jc(θ) at high field.

strategies.tuning strategies: Step-wise increase of heater temperature during multi-cycle deposition compensates for surface-temperature drop, keeping the first sub-layer near the buffer layer within the optimal growth window.
strategies.tuning effects: Preserves high-quality c-axis template at bottom interface, maintaining Tc ≈ 97 K and narrow ΔTc ≈ 0.6 K even in 3.3 µm film.

strategies.tuning strategies: Industrial MPMT-PLD maintains sharp (005) rocking curve (FWHM ≈ 1.5°) and (103) φ-scan (FWHM ≈ 2°) throughout 3.3 µm thickness; a-axis grains are minimized by dynamic temperature ramping.
strategies.tuning effects: Limits weak-link network, keeping texture comparable to 1.1 µm film.

strategies.tuning strategies: Multi-cycle deposition relaxes cumulative stress via intermittent thermal cycles; micro-strain rises only modestly from 0.21 % to 0.25 % when thickness triples.
strategies.tuning effects: Prevents crack formation and maintains mechanical integrity of thick coated conductor.

ExperimentTech.description: Industrial multi-plume multi-turn PLD (MPMT-PLD) at 300 Hz, 700–1000 mJ per pulse, 800–1000 mTorr O2, 1000–1100 °C for meter-scale deposition; structural analysis by XRD θ-2θ, ω, φ scans, Williamson-Hall micro-strain, Nelson-Riley lattice parameter; cross-sectional TEM/STEM-EDS for nanocolumn morphology; PPMS four-probe ρ(T) and magnetization Jc(B,θ) with Bean model; 18 T magnet transport at 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn pulsed laser deposition (MPMT-PLD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (θ-2θ, ω, φ scans), cross-sectional STEM/TEM with EDS, FIB sample preparation
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: PPMS four-probe resistivity, magnetization Jc via Bean model, 18 T transport Jc(θ) with 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion

Application.description: Thick 2G-HTS tapes for high-field magnets and rotating machinery require high in-field Jc and low anisotropy; the 3.3 µm BHO-doped EuBCO tape delivers ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T with reduced angular dependence, enabling compact, high-current cables and coils.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field accelerator magnets, fusion magnets, superconducting motors/generators
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc ≈ 5 MA/cm² at 4.2 K, 14 T (B//c); Jc anisropy ratio < 1.2 at 30 K, 5 T; Tc = 97 K, ΔTc = 0.6 K

MaterialSystem.description: EuBa2Cu3O7-δ (EuBCO) matrix co-doped with BaSnO3 (BSO) and BaHfO3 (BHO) forming BaSnxHf1-xO3 (BSHO) nanocolumns (~5 nm diameter, 2200 µm-2 areal density) aligned along the c-axis; c-lattice parameter 11.744 Å, in-plane texture 2.6°, out-of-plane texture 1.5%, micro-strain 0.29%.
MaterialSystem.dopants: BaSnO3 + BaHfO3 (3.5 mol% BHO + 4.5 mol% BSO)

TunningMethod.description: Synergistic co-doping of BSO and BHO during ultra-high-rate PLD exploits differential diffusion coefficients (Sn fast, Hf slow) to nucleate high-density semi-coherent BSHO nanocolumns that act as correlated pinning centers at intermediate fields and generate interfacial dislocations/oxygen vacancies serving as random pinning centers at high fields.

strategies.tuning strategies: Co-doping 3.5 mol% BHO + 4.5 mol% BSO to form BaSnxHf1-xO3 solid-solution nanocolumns; Sn provides high nucleation density while Hf limits radial growth, yielding 5 nm diameter columns at 2200 µm-2.
strategies.tuning effects: Increases correlated pinning matching field to 4.6–4.7 T and introduces semi-coherent interfaces that generate extra random pinning sites.

strategies.tuning strategies: Semi-coherent BSHO/EuBCO interfaces with two edge dislocations per a-/b-axis relieving 1-unit-cell mismatch, creating nanoscale strain fields and oxygen vacancies.
strategies.tuning effects: Produces dense random pinning centers that prevent Fp saturation up to 24 T, raising Fp to 990 GN m-3 at 4.2 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Reel-to-reel PLD on IBAD-MgO template maintains sharp biaxial texture (Δφ = 2.6°, Δω = 1.5°) despite >100 nm s-1 growth rate.
strategies.tuning effects: Preserves high critical current density (2.6 MA cm-2 at 77 K self-field) and enables columnar APCs to remain parallel to c-axis with <12° splay.

strategies.tuning strategies: Controlled micro-strain (0.29%) via epitaxial lattice mismatch between BSHO and EuBCO; strain drives formation of interfacial dislocations instead of macro-cracks.
strategies.tuning effects: Accommodates dopant-induced stress while avoiding current-blocking secondary-phase agglomerates.

strategies.tuning strategies: Liquid-assisted growth generates stripe-like pure EuBCO regions that interrupt nanocolumns, reducing effective matching field below theoretical 7.2 T.
strategies.tuning effects: Tunes vortex elasticity and suppresses over-pinning, maintaining high Jc(θ) anisotropy favorable for perpendicular-field applications.

ExperimentTech.description: Ultra-high-rate reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn PLD (>100 nm s-1) for 1 µm thick film deposition; cross-sectional & plan-view TEM/STEM-EDS for atomic-scale nanocolumn composition; 4-probe transport Jc(B,T,θ) up to 24 T and 4.2–77 K using 25 T cryogen-free magnet.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Reel-to-reel multi-plume multi-turn pulsed laser deposition (MPMT-PLD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: XRD θ–2θ/ω/φ scans, cross-sectional & plan-view TEM/STEM-EDS, Williamson–Hall nanostrain analysis
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe transport Jc(B,T,θ) in 18 T and 25 T superconducting magnets with rotatable cryostat

Application.description: High-field magnet applications (≥5 T, 50 K or ≥20 T, 20 K) require REBCO tapes with high in-field Jc and strong pinning force; co-doped EuBCO delivers unsaturated Fp = 990 GN m-3 at 24 T, 4.2 K and Jc = 4.0 MA cm-2 at 50 K, 3 T perpendicular field, outperforming commercial tapes.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field magnets for superconducting maglev, wind generators, compact fusion systems, and high-field NMR.
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(50 K, 3 T, ⊥) = 4.0 MA cm-2; Jc(4.2 K, 24 T, ⊥) = 4.2 MA cm-2; Fp(4.2 K, 24 T) = 990 GN m-3 (non-saturating)

MaterialSystem.description: Epitaxial (Y0.8RE'0.2-xRE''x)Ba2Cu3O7-y (YREBCO) thin films grown on SrTiO3 (STO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. The lattice maintains the orthorhombic YBCO structure while incorporating mixed rare-earth ions (Y, Gd, Yb, Dy, Ho, Sm, Nd) that create local strain fields and incidental (Y,RE',RE'')2O3 nanoparticles (≤14 nm) uniformly embedded within the superconducting matrix. The films exhibit high c-axis texture with rocking-curve FWHM as low as 0.2° when processed with liquid-assisted + layer-by-layer deposition.

TunningMethod.description: The study decouples competing effects of RE mixing by keeping growth temperature fixed at the YBCO optimum (790 °C). A moderate ion-size variance (2.31×10⁻⁴) in (Y0.8Gd0.1Yb0.1)Ba2Cu3O7-y maximizes Jc(20 K, 8 T) by balancing beneficial RE2O3 nanoparticle pinning against detrimental atomic-scale disorder. Liquid-phase (BaCu2O2) addition heals lattice disruption caused by nanoparticles, while layer-by-layer deposition improves cation uniformity and crystalline perfection, collectively doubling Jc compared to pure YBCO.

strategies.tuning strategies: Select moderate RE ion-size variance (Y0.8Gd0.1Yb0.1) to generate an optimal density of incidental (Y,Gd,Yb)2O3 nanoparticles without introducing excessive atomic disorder.
strategies.tuning effects: Yields ~1.5× higher Jc(20 K, 8 T) than pure YBCO; too high variance (Nd-containing) severely suppresses Jc despite more nanoparticles.

strategies.tuning strategies: Add 26 mol% BaCu2O2 liquid phase during PLD to promote rapid atomic diffusion, heal point/extended defects, and maintain coherent YREBCO/RE2O3 interfaces.
strategies.tuning effects: Reduces rocking-curve FWHM by ~30%, enabling nanoparticle pinning benefits to dominate over lattice disruption.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ layer-by-layer deposition (50 Hz laser pulsing with relaxation cycles) to enhance c-axis alignment and lateral uniformity of RE cations.
strategies.tuning effects: Further lowers FWHM(ω) and FWHM(2θ), producing the highest Jc(20 K, 8 T) = 3.75 MA cm⁻² among all processed films.

strategies.tuning strategies: Keep average RE ionic radius equal to Y³⁺ to minimize macroscopic lattice strain while allowing controlled local strain fields around nanoparticles.
strategies.tuning effects: Prevents global lattice distortion that would otherwise degrade long-range coherence and Jc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use liquid-assisted growth to reduce misorientation between YREBCO grains and suppress weak-link behavior across nanoparticle-influenced boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Improves inter-grain current flow, contributing to the overall 2× Jc enhancement at 8 T, 20 K.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were fabricated by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with three protocols: standard solid-state deposition (SSD), liquid-assisted PLD (+L), and layer-by-layer deposition (+LLD). Structural quality was assessed by X-ray diffraction (rocking curves, θ–2θ) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) for nanoparticle size/density. Critical current density was measured via four-probe transport on 25 µm-wide bridges using 0.2 µV cm⁻¹ criterion at 20 K in fields up to 10 T || c-axis.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD), liquid-assisted PLD, layer-by-layer deposition (LLD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), Raman spectroscopy
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe critical current density vs field (20 K, 0–10 T), transition temperature Tc

Application.description: Coated conductors operating at 20 K and high magnetic fields are required for compact fusion magnets and high-field inserts. The optimized YGdYb+L+LLD film delivers 3.75 MA cm⁻² at 8 T, 20 K, doubling the performance of reference YBCO and providing a superior template for further artificial pinning center integration.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Fusion reactor high-field toroidal field coils and insert magnets operating at ~20 K
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(20 K, 8 T) = 3.75 MA cm⁻², >1.5× that of pure YBCO films

MaterialSystem.description: c-axis oriented YBa2Cu3O7 (YBCO) epitaxial thin films grown on SrTiO3 (STO) buffer layers with 0–50 % CeO2 addition. The lattice mismatch is small (≈1 %), enabling coherent growth. CeO2 phase-separates into [001]-oriented nanowalls within STO, creating a nano-roughened template that triggers formation of BaCeO3 nanoparticles and dense threading screw dislocations (up to 150 μm⁻²) propagating along the c-axis.

TunningMethod.description: By engineering the buffer-layer chemistry and morphology, CeO2 nanowalls nucleate interfacial BaCeO3 nanoparticles that act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for threading screw dislocations. The dislocation density is tuned via CeO2 content (30 % vs 50 %) and deposition temperature (800 °C vs 850 °C), yielding one-dimensional natural pinning centers without sacrificing superconducting volume.

strategies.tuning strategies: Add 30–50 % CeO2 into STO buffer to induce phase separation into CeO2 nanowalls; subsequent Ce diffusion reacts with YBCO to form BaCeO3 nanoparticles at the interface.
strategies.tuning effects: Nanoparticles serve as nucleation seeds that multiply threading screw dislocations, increasing areal density from 20 to 150 μm⁻².

strategies.tuning strategies: Replace atomically flat STO surface with nano-roughened STO+CeO2 buffer covered by 8–25 nm BaCeO3 nanoparticles.
strategies.tuning effects: Rough interface geometrically forces dislocation generation, converting interface energy into linear defects that thread the entire YBCO thickness.

strategies.tuning strategies: Eliminate a-axis grains by CeO2-modified buffer; only c-axis YBCO observed in 1-μm-wide TEM foils.
strategies.tuning effects: Pure c-axis texture removes weak-link high-angle grain boundaries, ensuring dislocations remain the dominant pinning landscape.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit small lattice mismatch between YBCO and STO+CeO2 to maintain coherent growth while local strain fields around BaCeO3 precipitates drive dislocation formation.
strategies.tuning effects: Minimizes global residual stress, preventing film cracking, yet local strain concentrates at nanoparticles to nucleate dislocations.

strategies.tuning strategies: Suppress low-angle grain boundaries via optimized CeO2 nanowall spacing (~20 nm) that guides uniform YBCO nucleation.
strategies.tuning effects: Reduces correlated pinning competition; threading dislocations become sole strong 1D pins, raising Jc(65 K, 1 T) to match 3 vol % BSO nanorod reference.

ExperimentTech.description: Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) grown 300-nm YBCO on PLD STO+CeO2/LaAlO3; FIB prepared cross-section and plan-view TEM/STEM samples; Jc measured by 4-probe transport on 100 µm bridges in 65–77 K, 0–9 T perpendicular field.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition (KrF, 243 nm, 10 Hz, 200 mTorr O₂)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Cross-sectional & plan-view TEM, HR-TEM, STEM-EDX elemental mapping, selected-area electron diffraction, two-beam diffraction contrast
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) transport, 10 µV cm⁻¹ criterion

Application.description: High-performance coated conductors for superconducting magnets and cables require high in-field critical current density without artificial non-superconducting inclusions that reduce the current-carrying cross-section.
Application.ApplicationScenario: REBCO coated conductors for fusion magnets and compact cryo-cables operating at 65–77 K under 1–5 T perpendicular fields
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(65 K, 1 T) ≈ 3 MA cm⁻², matching 3 vol % BaSnO₃ nanorod-doped YBCO; Jc(77 K, 1 T) ≈ 1 MA cm⁻²

MaterialSystem.description: Granular 1:2:3 high-temperature superconductors ReBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ (Re = Y, Dy) with orthorhombic perovskite structure (space group Pmmm). Y-123 (a = 3.828 Å, b = 3.8947 Å, c = 11.7286 Å, Δ = 0.0172) is magnetically neutral (4f shell vacant), while Dy-123 (a = 3.8341 Å, b = 3.898 Å, c = 11.721 Å, Δ = 0.0165) contains magneto-active Dy³⁺ with filled 4f¹⁰ shell, introducing internal magnetic field Hint > 0. Both systems exhibit granular microstructure (~1 µm grains) separated by Josephson weak-link boundaries (~nm scale).

TunningMethod.description: The study exploits the intrinsic difference in 4f-shell filling between Y and Dy to tune the magnetic environment inside granular HTSC. By replacing non-magnetic Y with magnetic Dy, an internal magnetic field is introduced that cooperates with the external field to suppress the critical temperature of the Josephson medium (Tc2J) and expand the dissipative region Tc2J–Tc1g, thereby controlling phase-transition kinetics without altering crystal structure or oxygen content.

strategies.tuning strategies: Substitute magnetically neutral Y by magneto-active Dy to create internal magnetic field Hint > 0 inside Re-123 lattice; the filled 4f¹⁰ shell of Dy acts as localized magnetic scattering centers that cooperate with external field to enhance vortex penetration into weak links.
strategies.tuning effects: Tc2J drops from >77 K (Y-123) to 70.5 K (Dy-123) at only 250 Oe; the Josephson-medium existence window Tc2J–Tc1g widens by ~8 K, indicating stronger dissipation and reduced vortex-pinning efficiency.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain identical ceramic processing (950 °C, 24 h, 5 °C min⁻¹ cooling) for both compositions to ensure comparable grain size (~1 µm) and intergranular Josephson junctions; the sole variable is the magnetic state of the Re site, isolating the effect of Hint on weak-link dissipation.
strategies.tuning effects: Dy-123 exhibits earlier onset of resistivity at lower Hext owing to enhanced Josephson vortex nucleation at boundaries, while Y-123 retains zero resistance up to 1900 Oe at 77 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Deposit Ag contacts after final oxidation anneal (500 °C) to minimize contact resistance at ReBCO/Ag interface; identical contact protocol for both samples ensures that measured Tc shifts reflect bulk magnetic interaction rather than interface artifacts.
strategies.tuning effects: Contact resistance reduction enables accurate detection of subtle Tc2J shifts induced by internal field, allowing resolution of 0.5 K differences in transition temperature.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use slow cooling (≈5 °C min⁻¹) after oxidation anneal to relieve thermal stress and maintain identical orthorhombic distortion; slight decrease in rhombicity Δ for Dy-123 (0.0165 vs 0.0172) is accepted as secondary effect of Dy radius, not dominant factor in Tc suppression.
strategies.tuning effects: Stress relaxation ensures that observed Tc2J degradation is attributed to magnetic rather than mechanical origin, confirming Hint as the primary tuning parameter.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ identical uniaxial pressing (650 kg mm⁻²) to produce randomly oriented granular ceramics; absence of epitaxial texture guarantees that any anisotropic magnetic response arises solely from Dy 4f moments, not from crystallographic alignment.
strategies.tuning effects: Isotropic ceramic texture validates that Tc2J suppression is isotropic and linked to bulk 4f magnetism, providing clear evidence for intrinsic magnetic-field tuning of Josephson network.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples were synthesized by conventional solid-state ceramic route, certified via X-ray diffraction (DRON UM-1, Cu Kα, 2θ = 15–75°), and electrically characterized in a home-built cryostat equipped with Nd₂Fe₁₄B permanent-magnet pairs delivering 0–1900 Oe perpendicular field. Resistivity ρ(T) was recorded at constant transport current density j = 2 A cm⁻² (I = 10 mA) using four-probe DC method under field-cooled (FC) protocol with ultra-slow sweep 0.002–0.004 K s⁻¹ to ensure equilibrium vortex configuration.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Solid-state ceramic synthesis (950 °C, 24 h), uniaxial pressing (650 kg mm⁻²), oxidation anneal (500 °C, slow cool)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray powder diffraction (DRON UM-1, Cu Kα, Δ2θ = 0.01°), lattice-parameter refinement (accuracy 1e-4 Å)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe DC resistivity vs T in transverse magnetic field (0–1900 Oe, FC mode, j = 2 A cm⁻², dT/dt = 0.002–0.004 K s⁻¹)

Application.description: The work identifies that eliminating magneto-active rare-earth atoms from Re-123 granular HTSC is essential to preserve high critical current and low dissipation in liquid-nitrogen-cooled high-current devices. The finding provides a materials-selection rule for designing fault-current limiters, superconducting cables and magnets operating at 77 K under external magnetic fields.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled high-current cables, fault-current limiters and superconducting magnets requiring stable Tc > 77 K under 0.1–0.2 T stray fields
Application.ApplicationIndex: Critical temperature of Josephson medium Tc2J > 77 K at 250 Oe for Y-123 vs 70.5 K for Dy-123; zero-resistance temperature window expanded by ~8 K when magnetic Dy is avoided

MaterialSystem.description: REBCO (Rare-Earth Barium Copper Oxide) coated conductors on 50 µm Hastelloy substrate with 1.6 µm superconducting layer and 2.5 µm Ag stabilizer; CFD architecture introduces a patterned high-resistive amorphous layer (100–320 µΩ·cm²) between REBCO and Ag over 80 % of the 4 mm tape width, creating local current-flow diversion without altering the orthorhombic REBCO lattice.

TunningMethod.description: The study synergistically combines interface engineering (CFD layer) and cable architecture to multiply the normal-zone propagation velocity (NZPV) by 4–4.5 without degrading Ic. The CFD layer forces current to divert laterally into the Ag stabilizer during a quench, lengthening the current-transfer length and accelerating quench expansion; when integrated into a CORC® cable the absence of inter-layer insulation preserves current sharing while the helical geometry homogenizes the quench front.

strategies.tuning strategies: Insert a patterned high-interfacial-resistance amorphous layer (100–320 µΩ·cm²) between REBCO and Ag stabilizer over 80 % of tape width to force current diversion during quench, increasing current-transfer length and NZPV.
strategies.tuning effects: NZPV rises by factor 4–4.5 in both single tape and CORC® cable; no Ic degradation observed.

strategies.tuning strategies: Select 6.35 mm OD copper former with 6.9 mm total bending diameter to keep axial compressive strain below −1 %, preserving 75 % of Ic for CFD tapes and 68 % for regular tapes after winding.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables robust CORC® winding without critical-current loss; CFD tapes slightly more bend-tolerant.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use continuous reel-to-reel masking/etching to create sharp CFD boundaries while protecting low-Ri contact zones, avoiding lateral damage to REBCO grains and maintaining n-value ≈ 22.
strategies.tuning effects: Maintains high n-value and uniform Ic along meter-length tapes; no weak links introduced.

strategies.tuning strategies: Preserve original biaxial REBCO texture during CFD processing; no post-etch anneal required, keeping narrow Δω < 5° in-plane alignment.
strategies.tuning effects: Superconducting layer retains high Jc > 1.5e11 A·m⁻² at 77 K, ensuring cable-level performance.

strategies.tuning strategies: Electro-deposit 10 µm Cu pads at cable terminals to prevent In–Ag intermetallic consumption during soldering, preserving REBCO stoichiometry.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates terminal degradation; contact resistance < 1 µΩ·cm² maintained after multiple thermal cycles.

ExperimentTech.description: Meter-scale reel-to-reel CFD patterning (masking, chemical etching, unmasking, silver sputtering) was developed for continuous tape production. Critical current extracted with 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion using pulsed-current four-probe method; NZPV mapped via 5.9 mm-spaced pogo-pin PCB voltage taps on 16 cm cable section while quench triggered by local NdFeB magnet. Temperature controlled 67–77 K by pumped-LN₂ cryostat with ±0.05 K uniformity.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Reel-to-reel masking & wet etching to create CFD zones; CORC® cable winding on copper former with indium-soldered copper terminals
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: E–I power-law fitting with current-transfer-voltage subtraction; bending-diameter Ic retention tests; optical inspection of quench damage
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Pulsed-current Ic (1 µV cm⁻¹); multi-channel DAQ NZPV with 0.1 V threshold; PT100 temperature mapping

Application.description: Fast quench detection and self-protection of HTS magnets and fault-current-limiting power cables require NZPV high enough to generate detectable voltage before hot-spot formation. CFD CORC® cables deliver 4–4.5× higher NZPV (up to 0.35 m s⁻¹ at 1 kA, 77 K) while retaining 581 A (540 A after thermal cycle) critical current, enabling voltage-based protection within milliseconds and homogeneous current limitation.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field fusion & accelerator magnets, electric-aircraft superconducting transmission lines, fault-current limiters
Application.ApplicationIndex: Ic = 581 A (540 A) at 77 K, self-field; NZPV = 9e-4 I^1.89 m s⁻¹ (I in A); Jc ≈ 1.5e11 A·m⁻² per tape

MaterialSystem.description: REBa2Cu3O7-y (RE123) superconductors with 3–5 rare-earth elements (Eu, Gd, Y, Er, Yb, Nd, La) homogeneously sharing the RE site; lattice parameters increase linearly with average RE3+ ionic radius (1.029–1.076 Å); nanoscale stacking faults (SFs) are generated inside grains due to incomplete diffusion during peritectic reaction, acting as effective vortex-pinning planes; all samples retain orthorhombic structure without phase separation.

TunningMethod.description: By systematically increasing the number of RE elements (3→5) and their average ionic radius while keeping unified processing, the study decouples the roles of configurational entropy (ΔSmix) and ionic size on Tc, SC volume fraction and Jc. The highest-Jc sample (Eu0.25Gd0.25Y0.25Er0.25)BCO combines a 98 % SC volume fraction with dense nanoscale SFs introduced by medium-entropy mixing, demonstrating that composition-driven defect engineering dominates Jc rather than orthorhombicity.

strategies.tuning strategies: Introduce 3–5 equi-atomic RE elements at the RE site to raise configurational entropy (ΔSmix = 1.10–1.60 R), promoting nanoscale stacking-fault formation that act as strong flux-pinning centers.
strategies.tuning effects: Sample 2#-EuGdYEr attains the highest self-field Jc = 373 kA cm-2 at 4.2 K and retains >10 kA cm-2 at 5 T, correlating with 98 % SC volume fraction and dense SFs.

strategies.tuning strategies: Select RE combinations avoiding La (prone to Ba-site substitution) to suppress local Tc degradation; instead use Eu/Gd/Y/Er/Nd mixtures that keep Tc > 90 K.
strategies.tuning effects: Eliminates La-induced weak links; samples without La show narrower superconducting transitions and higher SC volume fractions.

strategies.tuning strategies: Sinter bulk pellets 5 °C above peritectic temperature (Tp) to generate a minute CuO-rich liquid phase that wets grain boundaries and accelerates densification without secondary phases.
strategies.tuning effects: Relative density reaches 84–92 %, reducing weak-link grain-boundary resistance and supporting high inter-grain Jc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit positive correlation between average RE3+ radius and Tp (1032→1072 °C) to enlarge processing window; larger ions lower lattice strain and increase oxygen-vacancy formation energy, retarding decomposition.
strategies.tuning effects: Enables stable single-phase synthesis and post-annealing at 400 °C for full oxygenation, ensuring robust 90 K-class superconductivity.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ identical solid-state sintering and oxygen annealing protocols for all compositions to maintain similar micron-scale platelet grains and low-angle boundaries, isolating the effect of RE mixing on Jc.
strategies.tuning effects: Morphology remains uniform across samples; observed Jc differences are therefore attributed to intragrain pinning (SFs) and SC volume rather than grain-boundary degradation.

ExperimentTech.description: Conventional solid-state sintering in flowing air was used to prepare both powder and bulk samples; phase purity, lattice parameters and actual cation ratios were quantified by XRD-Rietveld and EDS; thermal stability was mapped via DSC-TG; nanoscale stacking faults were resolved by HRTEM and FFT; superconducting transition temperature and critical current density were extracted from PPMS magnetometry (ZFC/FC and M-H loops) using extended Bean model.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: solid-state sintering, twice calcination at 940 °C, uniaxial pressing (250 MPa), oxygen annealing 400 °C 48 h
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: XRD-Rietveld refinement, DSC-TG, FE-SEM-EDS, HRTEM-FFT, FIB lift-out
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: PPMS magnetometry (ZFC/FC, M-H), Bean-model Jc calculation at 4.2 K & 77 K

Application.description: Bulk RE123 with multi-RE mixing delivers high Jc above 350 kA cm-2 at 4.2 K and >10 kA cm-2 at 5 T, suitable for compact cryo-magnets, superconducting magnetic coils, flywheel energy storage and maglev systems operating at liquid-helium temperature.
Application.ApplicationScenario: superconducting magnetic coils, flywheel energy storage, superconducting maglev
Application.ApplicationIndex: self-field Jc = 373 kA cm-2 at 4.2 K, Jc(5 T, 4.2 K) > 10 kA cm-2, Tc > 90 K

MaterialSystem.description: YBa2Cu3Oy (YBCO) matrix with self-assembled BaHfO3 (BHO) nanorods grown epitaxially on IBAD-MgO buffered metallic tapes; BHO forms 5–10 nm diameter c-axis-aligned nanorods that act as correlated flux-pinning centers.

TunningMethod.description: A Bayesian-optimization-guided loop simultaneously varied Y stoichiometry and substrate temperature to maximize Jc(20 K, 9 T). The algorithm revealed that Y-poor (x = 0.9) compositions grown at 870 °C drive higher supersaturation, producing denser, thinner and slightly tilted BHO nanorods that collectively strengthen low-T flux pinning.

strategies.tuning strategies: Reduce Y content from stoichiometric 1.0 to 0.9 to increase growth supersaturation, which refines BHO nanorod diameter and raises nanorod number density from 2.1e3 to 3.5e3 μm-2.
strategies.tuning effects: Finer and denser nanorods enhance correlated pinning, lifting Jc at 20 K, 9 T by ~40 % relative to Y1.0 film.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain substrate temperature at 870 °C to secure epitaxial YBCO/BHO interface while permitting slight nanorod tilt (9–11°) that enlarges the effective pinning volume.
strategies.tuning effects: Optimized interface preserves high structural quality and minimizes weak-link grain boundaries, keeping self-field Jc intact while improving in-field performance.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use IBAD-MgO template to impose sharp biaxial texture; Y-poor growth conditions do not degrade out-of-plane Δω nor in-plane Δφ, ensuring long current percolation paths.
strategies.tuning effects: Strong texture reduces high-angle grain boundaries, so the gain in pinning directly translates to higher engineering Jc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Lower Y content slightly contracts the YBCO lattice, compensating tensile thermal stress generated during cool-down from 870 °C to 20 K.
strategies.tuning effects: Reduced residual stress suppresses micro-crack formation, retaining film integrity and stabilizing Jc at cryogenic temperature.

strategies.tuning strategies: Higher supersaturation under Y0.9 promotes island coalescence at earlier growth stage, decreasing porosity along grain boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Cleaner grain boundaries lower the inter-granular weak-link density, improving current transfer across the coated conductor.

ExperimentTech.description: Pulsed-laser deposition with KrF laser on IBAD-MgO tapes was used for film growth; micro-bridges were patterned by UV laser marking. Microstructure was inspected by cross-sectional and plan-view STEM, while Jc–B and Jc–θ were measured with a four-probe DC method in PPMS. A custom Bayesian-optimization code (BOXVIA) employing Gaussian-process regression and Expected-Improvement acquisition guided the sequential experiments.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM)
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: DC four-probe I–V in Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS)

Application.description: Compact fusion magnets and high-field inserts require REBCO tapes that carry >0.4 MA cm-2 at 20 K and 9 T; the optimized YBCO+BHO conductor meets this target and exhibits higher irreversibility field than standard Y1.0 tapes.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field fusion magnets operating at 20 K, 9 T
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc(20 K, 9 T, B//c) > 0.4 MA cm-2

MaterialSystem.description: YBa₂Cu₃O₇ (YBCO) superconducting films deposited on IBAD-MgO buffered metallic substrates or single-crystal SrTiO₃. The films grow epitaxially with c-axis orientation; IBAD substrates provide biaxial texture (Δϕ ≈ 1.7–3.6°) while SrTiO₃ gives nearly single-crystalline lattice matching. Natural linear defects (dislocations) and occasional low-angle grain boundaries (~2°) act as vortex-pinning centers. No intentional chemical doping is introduced.

TunningMethod.description: Critical current density Jc is optimized by data-driven adjustment of substrate temperature Tsub across different PLD chambers. Transfer learning converts equipment-specific Tsub scales into an equivalent coordinate space, while physics-aided modeling (1/Jc³) unifies magnetic-field dependences. The approach simultaneously accounts for non-numerical factors (chamber design, substrate type) and microscopic pinning mechanisms.

strategies.tuning strategies: Post-annealing in flowing oxygen at 400 °C or oxygenation during cooling is used to control oxygen stoichiometry, thereby tuning carrier concentration and Tc without altering cation composition.
strategies.tuning effects: Optimized carrier concentration raises Tc and indirectly enlarges the Tsub window for high Jc.

strategies.tuning strategies: Selection of IBAD substrates with low in-plane mosaic spread (Δϕ ≤ 2°) and growth at Tsub ≥ 860 °C reduces grain-boundary weak-link density, suppressing Jc degradation at low magnetic fields.
strategies.tuning effects: Low-angle boundaries shift the crossover field below 0.05 T, restoring high Jc at self-field and 77 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use of CeO₂-terminated IBAD templates or atomically flat SrTiO₃ ensures epitaxial lattice matching, minimizing interfacial disorder that would otherwise reduce current flow area.
strategies.tuning effects: Smooth interfaces promote uniform nucleation and high-texture YBCO, increasing the effective cross-section for supercurrent.

strategies.tuning strategies: IBAD process itself imparts biaxial texture to the metallic substrate; subsequent homo-epitaxial buffer layers replicate this texture into the YBCO film, aligning ab-planes over meter length.
strategies.tuning effects: Strong texture reduces high-angle grain boundaries, raising the percolative Jc and its uniformity along coated-conductor tapes.

strategies.tuning strategies: Matching thermal expansion between IBAD substrate stack and YBCO, combined with controlled cooling rate, limits tensile residual stress that could generate cracks at high Tsub or thick films.
strategies.tuning effects: Reduced residual stress preserves film integrity and maintains high Jc (>3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K, 0 T) over 200–250 nm thickness.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples are fabricated by four distinct pulsed-laser deposition systems (R&D and reel-to-reel). Key innovations are (i) transfer-learning-augmented Gaussian-process regression that merges small datasets from different chambers and (ii) physics-aided modeling (1/Jc³) to extrapolate Jc(B) with only a reference field dataset. Characterization includes X-ray φ-scans for texture and four-probe transport for Jc(B,T).
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed-laser deposition (KrF, 246 nm) on IBAD-MgO/CeO₂ metallic substrates and single-crystal SrTiO₃; reel-to-reel and static R&D chambers.
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction ω–2θ, φ-scans (Δϕ); scanning of plume imaging for qualitative chamber-to-chamber comparison.
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Four-probe critical current density Jc(B,T) at 65–77 K, 0–9 T (B//c); resistive Tc measurement in Physical Property Measurement System.

Application.description: Coated conductors require kilometer-length tapes carrying >3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K and self-field, with predictable performance in external magnetic fields up to 3 T for motors, generators and fusion magnets. The integrated GPR-TL-PAM model enables rapid process transfer from pilot to production PLD lines while maintaining Jc targets.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Second-generation high-temperature-superconducting wires for coated-conductor applications (power cables, fault-current limiters, high-field inserts).
Application.ApplicationIndex: Critical current density Jc > 3 MA cm⁻² at 77 K, 0 T; predictable Jc(B) at 65 K up to 3 T with R² ≥ 0.81 after transfer learning.

MaterialSystem.description: EuBa2Cu3Oy (EuBCO) films grown by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) on IBAD-MgO buffered metallic substrates; films contain coherent BaHfO3 (BHO) inclusions that evolve from 4.5 nm nanoparticles at 1.9 vol% to splayed nanorods at 4.8 vol%. Undoped films host ~20 nm Eu2O3 precipitates, high-density c-axis dislocations at grain boundaries, and twin boundaries, yielding correlated disorder landscape.

TunningMethod.description: Vortex dynamics are engineered by tuning the morphology and volume fraction of coherent BHO inclusions (0–4.8 vol%) inside PLD-EuBCO. Increasing BHO boosts Jc via strong pinning but simultaneously accelerates vortex creep by enabling double-kink excitations along nanorods; undoped EuBCO exhibits intrinsically slow creep due to dense dislocation networks and fine grain structure. Optimal Jc is reached at 2.8 vol% BHO where large-bundle creep or a Bose-glass state is established.

strategies.tuning strategies: Introduce 1.9–4.8 vol% coherent BaHfO3 inclusions that self-assemble into nanoparticles/nanorods, creating strong pinning centers with diameter ~2ξab–4ξab.
strategies.tuning effects: Jc at 1.8 K rises 3.2× (self-field) and 6.2× (5 T) versus undoped film; power-law exponent α drops from 0.58 to 0.22, confirming crossover to strong-pinning regime.

strategies.tuning strategies: BHO addition doubles average grain size, reducing grain-boundary area and dislocation density at boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Lower grain-boundary density decreases weak-link losses, but residual dislocations still provide background pinning that competes with BHO nanorods.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain epitaxial PLD growth on IBAD-MgO/Gd2Zr2O7/Y2O3/LaMnO3/CeO2 buffered Hastelloy; optimize deposition temperature (1055 °C with BHO, 1150 °C without) and post-anneal O2 temperature (250–350 °C) to achieve near-optimal hole doping (p ≈0.152).
strategies.tuning effects: Preserves c-axis texture and coherent BHO/matrix interface, ensuring nanorod alignment along c-axis for maximal pinning anisotropy.

strategies.tuning strategies: Preserve sharp biaxial texture of EuBCO via PLD; BHO nanorods grow coherently within matrix maintaining cube-on-cube relationship.
strategies.tuning effects: Minimizes high-angle grain boundaries, enabling persistent high Jc up to 60 K and 5 T; correlated disorder promotes Bose-glass state evidenced by μ ≈7/9.

strategies.tuning strategies: Exploit lattice mismatch between BHO and EuBCO to create localized strain fields around nanorods, supplementing core pinning.
strategies.tuning effects: Strain fields enhance pinning energy U0, but excessive BHO (>2.8 vol%) increases nanorod splay, facilitating double-kink excitations and faster creep (S rises from 0.015 to 0.025 at 30 K, 1 T).

ExperimentTech.description: Samples synthesized by PLD with in-situ BHO incorporation; microstructure mapped by cross-sectional and plan-view TEM/STEM/EDS to quantify inclusion size, shape, and separation. Critical current density Jc(B,T) extracted from magnetization loops using Bean model. Vortex creep rate S and glassy exponent μ determined from 1-hour magnetic relaxation measurements fitted to collective-creep interpolation formula.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with in-situ BaHfO3 co-deposition; post-anneal O2 treatment at 250–350 °C.
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-angle annular dark-field STEM, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS).
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Quantum Design MPMS3 SQUID magnetometry (hysteresis loops and magnetic relaxation); Bean critical-state analysis for Jc; creep data fitting to extract S and μ.

Application.description: Coated conductors for high-field magnets and power devices require high in-field Jc and minimal vortex creep at 20–77 K. EuBCO+BHO films deliver Jc ≈31 MA cm-2 at 1.8 K, 5 T and retain Jc ≈2 MA cm-2 at 60 K, 1 T, outperforming MOD-(Y,Gd)BCO at elevated temperatures while revealing creep penalty above 2.8 vol% BHO.
Application.ApplicationScenario: High-field (>5 T) superconducting magnets and fault-current limiters operating at 20–65 K.
Application.ApplicationIndex: Jc = 31 MA cm-2 at 1.8 K, 5 T; Jc = 2 MA cm-2 at 60 K, 1 T; creep rate S = 0.015 (undoped) vs 0.025 (4.8 vol% BHO) at 30 K, 1 T.

MaterialSystem.description: Cu-rich YBa2Cu3O7−δ (Cu-YBCO) epitaxial films grown by PLD from a highly off-stoichiometric Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 target. Films are c-axis oriented (c ≈ 1.169 nm) and contain epitaxially embedded cubic-phase domains dispersed in the orthorhombic YBCO matrix without granular particles.

TunningMethod.description: Cu-excess introduces epitaxial cubic domains that act as artificial pinning centers, enhancing flux pinning without creating granular defects. The domains form uniformly throughout the film, improving JC and Birr near 77 K while maintaining surface smoothness required for nano-lithography.

strategies.tuning strategies: Employ a highly off-stoichiometric Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 target to introduce excess Cu that substitutes on Ba sites and precipitates as nanoscale cubic domains.
strategies.tuning effects: Creates epitaxial non-superconducting domains that pin vortices without granular particles, raising JC by 150 % and Birr by 20 % at 80 K.

strategies.tuning strategies: Grow films on lattice-matched LSAT substrates at 780 °C to ensure clean epitaxial interfaces and minimize interfacial strain.
strategies.tuning effects: Achieves strain-relaxed high-quality epitaxy (Δc < 0.001 nm) and suppresses secondary phases, enabling smooth surfaces for device patterning.

strategies.tuning strategies: Maintain pure c-axis orientation via optimized PLD conditions (1 J cm−2, 100 mTorr O2) to align Cu-rich domains coherently within the YBCO matrix.
strategies.tuning effects: Produces four-fold symmetric in-plane texture (φ-scan) and eliminates high-angle grain boundaries, preserving high inter-grain JC.

strategies.tuning strategies: Use 40 nm thickness—above critical thickness—to fully relax epitaxial strain on STO, LAO and LSAT substrates.
strategies.tuning effects: Avoids strain-induced defect formation and ensures uniform distribution of cubic pinning centers throughout the film thickness.

strategies.tuning strategies: Eliminate granular particles by controlling Cu excess level and post-annealing (400 °C, 1 h, 700 Torr O2), avoiding conventional APC-related grain boundaries.
strategies.tuning effects: Removes detrimental grain-boundary weak links, yielding smooth surfaces (RMS < 1 nm) compatible with sub-100 nm lithography for microwave devices.

ExperimentTech.description: Samples prepared by 248 nm KrF PLD on STO, LAO, LSAT; characterized by XRD, HR-TEM, SEM-EDS for structure/composition; superconducting properties measured with PPMS-AC transport and VSM.
ExperimentTech.FabricationTech: Pulsed laser deposition (248 nm KrF, 1 J cm−2, 100 mTorr O2, 780 °C)
ExperimentTech.CharacterizationTech: X-ray diffraction, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy with EDS
ExperimentTech.MeasurementTech: Quantum Design PPMS ac-transport and vibrating sample magnetometer

Application.description: High-performance HTS thin-film devices operating at 77 K require high JC and Birr together with smooth surfaces for nano-patterning; Cu-YBCO meets these demands without granular defects.
Application.ApplicationScenario: Microwave filters and integrated HTS circuits on LSAT substrates
Application.ApplicationIndex: JC(80 K, 0 T) ≈ 3.7 MA cm−2; JC(80 K, 1.2 T) 1.6× higher than pure YBCO; Birr(80 K) enhanced by 20 %
